articles.title: Norfair - Super Metroid Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The easternmost Brinstar elevator takes you down to Norfair, which will put you on a course to get you an upgrade item that lets you easily jump up to higher
articles.body:
The easternmost Brinstar elevator takes you down to Norfair, which will put you on a course to get you an upgrade item that lets you easily jump up to higher up ledges: the High Jump Boots.

Drop down from the elevator and make your way to the very bottom. You'll pass a few doors that lead to areas you can't yet complete.

You'll find a new enemy species here, crawling on the platforms and walls.

Sova look like the fire version of Geemers. Native to Norfair, they are faster and deal more damage when you collide with them.

There will be a red door to your left and a blue door to your right on top of a destructible rock walkway.

First, enter the room behind the blue door: it's your first Norfair Save Room. Save your data and exit back out.

Go through the red door on the opposite side.

Pick up the Energy Tank sitting in the middle of the room.

Walk to the end of the room and fall through one of the two brittle blocks, then roll yourself up and follow the tunnel until you reach a blue door.

Watch out for the crawling Sova. Drop a bomb before it can touch you to clear the way.

Get the Missile Tank Early: Sequence Break Alert!

This is just a small sequence break opportunity that is honestly not worth your time. There is a Missile Tank up above that you can get to right now by wall jumping up twice. You can also Bomb Jump up -- from either side of the Missile cave (there is a hidden passage from the right side). But it's easiest to just return in a minute, with your new power-up on foot.

Open the blue door to enter a room with a Chozo Statue holding an item on the other side of a metal wall.

Angle up or jump to shoot the metal blocks at the top to open the path. Three blocks can be destroyed to let you easily jump over the hurdle and get to the prize.

Shoot the sphere the statue is holding to reveal and then collect the High-Jump Boots . You can now jump 1 1/2 times higher!

When you exit the blue hatch (hi-)jump to the ledge above and jump again to reach the tunnel which will give you access to a Missile Expansion . We described a way to get there via Wall or Bomb Jumping above, but this way is much, much easier.

Use a bomb to make a tunnel in the wall behind where the Missile Tank was and exit through the blue door you came through earlier.

Back in the tall cave, climb up, shooting the Sovas on the way, as needed.

Take the Norfair elevator back up to Brinstar.

Samus should backtrack now to get the Spazer gun upgrade.

The Spazer is hidden in a secret room above the large room in the southeastern corner of the Brinstar map.

When you arrive in Brinstar, take the blue door to the left and run through the three cave segments to get back to the waterlogged rooms with the Yapping Maws.

Carefully navigate the platforms to go to the far left side of the room. Don't open the blue door -- stop in front of it.

There is a cracked block in the ceiling. Aim up and shoot the cracked block, then jump up with your newly acquired Hi-Jump Boots into the concealed area. Land on the ledge to the right, then jump again.

When you reach the top, use the Morph Ball and drop a Bomb in front of the first cracked rock to blow it up. Caution! Do not attempt to bomb the second cracked block in the narrow passage. It's a trap that would send you falling down into a waiting Maw.

Instead, crouch and shoot the cracked block, then roll through the passage to get to the green door. Open it and enter.

Within, you will find a Chozo Statue holding a glowing sphere. Shoot the sphere to get the Spazer .

This Beam upgrade triples Samus's shot, dealing a much wider area of damage and making it easier to hit enemies and destructible blocks. A single shot causes 40 HP damage, double the regular Beam's attack, which damages 20 HP.

Now head back down and to the right, the way you came, to the elevator that leads to Norfair.

When you reach the elevator, do not go down.

Instead, crouch down and shoot the block in the wall opposite the blue door with a Super Missile. Enter the passage created using the Morph Ball ability.

You will now be in a small blue room. To the top right there is an opening in the form of a monster's head. Thanks to the Hi-Jump Boots, you can now easily jump up to it. The monster's mouth leads to a passage. Enter the passage and follow it until you reach a blue door.

Enter through the blue door to get to a shaft with green walls and red girders. Bomb or shoot the ground to make an opening on the left side and drop down.

There will be a locked gray door at the bottom which you cannot enter.

Gray doors are usually unlocked/turned blue by shooting all the enemies in a room. This particular gray door won't unlock even if you shoot all three Zeela in this room. Instead, it requires you to take down the area's boss, Kraid.

Bomb the wall opposite the door and enter the hidden horizontal passage. At the end of this passage there will be a blue hatch in the ceiling.

This damaged and overgrown room houses three green Kihunters. Charge your beam or use Missiles to defeat them fast.

Head to the rightmost end of this room until you can see a couple of steps leading to a dead end.

Bomb the bottom step to reveal a passageway which leads to a Save Room.

Save your data and head back into the secret passage leading to the room with the steps.

You may notice that there's a destructible block in the middle of the hidden passage, on the pipe element leading up. This block can only be destroyed by standing on it (in other word, it's an exit, not an entrance). The entrance to that secret area is outside the passage at the top of the wall -- but you need a Power Bomb to open it. So make a mental note for later.

Half-way through this room you will see a damaged piece of ground (it is black unlike the rest of the green surroundings).

Bomb this patch of ground to reveal a passage that will lead to a blue door. Enter the blue door, which will lead to a long green room.

Kill the Space Pirates within this room. They are the green kind, which have 90 HP, so three Spazer shots will do the trick.

As you approach the far side, thorns will be fired at Samus. Dodge these by jumping over them until you reach a Kraid-like enemy.

This Kraid baby is a preview of what's to come. Standing about as tall as Samus, Mini-Kraid fires spikes in a horizontal trajectory. Jump over them, then blast it with a few missiles. Mini-Kraids will drop crucial Super Missile refills. There is only one Mini-Kraid in the game.

Just four missile hits will take down the miniature version of Kraid.

The gray door behind it will unlock. Enter the room the Mini-Kraid was guarding.

When you enter the next room, aim up and shoot the two block above the door you entered from. Jump up through the hole and then continue up the large steps to unlock and enter through the green door.

You will discover a room with two recharge stations to refill both your Energy and your Missiles.

Head back down to the room, and proceed onwards. Jump over the spikes and use the metal platforms to stand on.

You'll see a dead soldier on the ground, being devoured by Sbugs. They are harmless and will scatter as you approach.

At the end of this room is an eye-like enemy blocking access to a hatch. It's known as a Gadora.

This enemy, surely named for the fact that it's gua rding a door has 300 HP and will fire energy orbs at Samus. Take it out fast to open the door it's blocking. Gadora are usually found on doors that have a significant battle behind them -- so heed the warning and make sure you're stocked up on ammo, energy, and have recently saved.

Wait until the enemy opens its eye and then shoot with a missile. Three direct hits will destroy it and make the door accessible. Enter the next room.

Initially, the room is empty -- and it looks like you can't progress. But the door behind you is shut. Wait a few seconds and your foe will appear.

Kraid is a room-sized dragon that will damage you if you come in contact with it -- but it also spits rocks and tries to hit you with its claws. To destroy Kraid, shoot it in the face with the Spazer, then, when it opens its mouth fire a Super Missile or Missile into its mouth.

One Super Missile Shot will trigger its second phase.

The hit will cause it to show its full size, as it will rise up from the thorny ground. Since his face is now high up, you'll need to use the Hi-Jump Boots to leap up to two platforms.

Kraid's attacks will change. The rocks are no more, instead its weak attack are spikes it shoots from its belly, which fly boomerang-like through the air. You can shoot them to get more missiles.

Your main objective is to dodge attacks so that you don't fall into the spikes below. Kraid will move forward and backward. Follow and retreat, and keep an eye on its hands. It will now fire its claws at you. You can jump over them and even ride them (you don't take damage when standing on them).

Keep firing the Spazer at Kraid's face to cause it to roar, then switch and follow up with your missiles. After a few hits, Kraid will change color to show that you're causing real damage.

A Super Missile will cause 300 damage to this 1000 HP beast, so you only need a total of four direct hits, or three, and a regular missile, to bring it down.

General of the Space Pirates, Kraid is one of Samus's archenemies. Kraid has three different attack types. The rocks it spits and its belly projectiles cause 2 damage, while its claws deal 10. Coming into contact with its body causes the most damage, 20 HP, so keep your distance. Shoot Kraid's face to make it flash its eyes red and open its mouth. Then shoot it with Super Missiles.

When you defeat it, refill your health and ammo with whatever it drops.

After you have defeated Kraid, head through the now open door to the right. Inside, you will find your first major suit upgrade: the Varia-Suit.

Head back the way you came. Go refill your energy and missiles at the two recharge stations, then use the Zeb pipe to get your Super Missiles up to five. Continue onward. The Mini-Kraid will have respawned, as have all the other enemies. Blast them. You can also step at the Save Station again.

When you reach the green shaft from earlier, the door that was previously locked and gray is now flashing.

Open the door and enter, but get ready to fight an unusual foe.

These bat-rat-reptile looking hoppers like to attach themselves to Samus and drain her energy. You can freeze them, when you have proper hardware, but once they latch on, roll up in a ball and drop bombs while rolling to both sides (staying stationary will result in a bomb jump and not actually damage the enemy).

Defeat the energy-draining Beetoms by rolling into a ball and dropping some bombs while rolling back and forth. But the empty-looking room is not actually empty. Shoot the fourth block from the left in the ceiling to reveal an Energy Tank .

Now head back to the elevator which leads to Norfair.

Now that you are equipped with the Varia Suit, Samus can enter the high temperature rooms within Norfair.

Take the elevator down, then drop down and enter to the first blue door to your right.

When you enter the room you will be facing a wall. There are Sovas crawling around that you can shoot for ammo refills. Bomb the ground under you feet to blow up two blocks and drop down.

Run to the far side of the room until you are facing a wall and can proceed no further. On the way, you'll encounter a new type of hopper.

This small hopper-type has spikes and can be tough to avoid due to its erratic hopping. There's a bigger variety ahead, too, but this one can be taken down with just two charged shots.

Jump to the ledge above, jump again to the next ledge, and proceed through the red door to your right.

Within this room there are a variety of enemies, including a new type you haven't seen before.

These blue-eyed, owl-looking flyers float up and swoop down to attack. Stay clear of their path and blast them with two charged shots.

There are also pockets of lava which should be avoided as they rapidly drain health.

Work your way towards the far right of the room using the rocky platforms and jumping over the small rock pillars.

Missile in the Lava: Sequence Break Alert!

You don't yet have the ability to jump into lava and not get hurt. Do you care? This is technically a sequence break, since you can collect it safely later, but there is no special skill required, so we consider now the right time to pick it up. If you don't mind losing 60 or so HP, you jump into the second lava pool from the right, roll up into the Morph Ball, and drop a bomb in the lower right corner to reveal a hidden Missile Expansion.

You'll take damage the entire time that you're in the lava, but if you had plenty of energy, that's a small price to pay to get some more missiles early.

When you can go no further drop down to the ground below, to your right you will see a green door. Blast it with a Super Missile and enter.

This room is filled with lava -- and the all that seismic activity is shaking your screen. Use the series of platforms and jump from one to the next to make it across the room. The lava will rise as you progress, but it won't go higher than the platforms, don't worry.

These ray-like creatures love to live near lava. They rapidly jump up and down in a predictable pattern. Low jumps follow a single high jump. These armored nuisances can be blown up with a Super Missile, or frozen and used as stepping stones.

Don't waste your precious Super Missiles on the Squeept jumping out of the lava. Avoid them.

The seahorse-like Dragons can be more annoying. Take them out with a few well-placed missiles.

These seahorses -- or rather, lavahorses, emerge from the fiery liquid and try to take potshots at you, which can cause you to miss a jump and land you in the lava. Avoid their projectiles and shoot them with missiles to clear the path.

When you reach the other side of the room leave through the blue door.

You will now be in an area with green bubble-like blocks. Jump on to the ledge immediately above the blue door you just entered through.

Open the blue door and enter -- it leads to a Save Room. Save your data and exit.

Bomb Jump to a Missile: Sequence Break Alert!

Are you good at bomb jumping? There's a green door at the top of this room that you can get to by bomb jumping up from the bubble steps near the entrance. Don't worry if you can't make it yet -- you'll be able to return later and get it very easily. If you make it, blast the green door open, enter, take down the Geruta, and collect your missiles.

You can continue to sequence break by bomb jumping up to the other exits on the right, too.

Drop back down to the ground level, run across the room -- past the metallic pillars with heads -- to the wall farthest away from the entrance that got you here.

Samus will fall through a hole in the ground. On the first ledge Samus falls on, bomb the pipe block to her right to get to a lower level.

On this level bomb the pipe block to her left, causing her to fall again.

On the final level bomb the pipe block to her right.

You fall into a small room. Drop past the flying Ripper II and jump to the left, over the spikes, to grab another Missile Tank .

Exit this area the way you came, shooting the blocks and jumping out. Head back to the metallic pillars with the mounted heads.

Bomb the block at the center of the two pillars.

When you fall to the lower level, bomb the center block and enter the pipe.

There is only one route that can be followed within the pipe, so bomb any Sovas and blocks in the way until you exit the pipe in a room with two blue doors.

Enter the hatch on the ground. You will fall on to a platform.

Jump down until you come to a blue door to your right. In here, enemies will continuously spawn from a hole in the ground. Shoot them to refill your Missiles and Energy.

Another variety of flying bug that will continue to spawn until you leave, Gamets appear in larger groups that fan out and can be used to quickly refill health and ammo.

Drop down from the ledges until you come to a second blue hatch to your right and enter.

This is another lava filled room -- but before you hop across the platforms, familiarize yourself with the two new enemies you'll encounter here.

This fiery beast resembles a fireball with a face. It flies about lava-filled areas and causes 50 damage on contact. A single charge beam will destroy them.

Multiviola -- aka, the flying fire faceballs -- are easily destroyed. The fire columns, also known as Magdollite, put up much more of a fight. There's little to gain for spending the time to shoot them, so they're best avoided.

Magdollites are green-eyed lava snakes that rise out of the molten rock and form a column, then launch fire at you, horizontally. Despite their low HP, you'll need high fire power, such as Super Missile, to bring them down.

Use the platforms to make your way across the room to a blue door on the far side. The above-mentioned fire enemies will reach out of the lava and fire at Samus. Dodge these attacks and shoot the other Multiviola enemies within the room. Exit through the blue door.

You will enter a room with a blue door facing Samus and another new "face".

Related to the fire-type Multiviola, these blue energy balls show their faces in rocky areas. They follow along walls and platforms, similar to the crawler-types in other regions. Given their low HP and attack, they're more of a nuisance than an enemy you should take seriously. With one exception: they reliably drop Power Bomb refills.

Proceed through the blue door and work your way through the next lava-filled room.

You have to be quick here as the lava level raises and will kill Samus. When you get to the end of the room there will be an enemy situated on a wall. These alien heads are known as Fune -- and there'll be more of them in a second.

These alien heads stick out of walls and shoot glowing, blue fireballs at you. You can shoot them with Super Missiles, but it's best to just keep moving on, jumping over the projectiles, and avoiding them.

Roll under it in Morph Ball form, through through a small tunnel, and into a vertical shaft.

The lava keeps rising, so keep moving. Shoot the over-head blocks and jump up. There's a series of ledges here which alternate from left to right, while the walls are lined with more Fune spitters.

Work your way up the ledges while jumping over and ducking under the projectiles until you come to a blue door to your left. Exit through the door.

In this room there will be a flying creature with a platform on its back, known as a Tripper.

Not every creature in Super Metroid is out to kill Samus. These spaceship-esque flyers let you stand on their "platform" and can carry you to places you couldn't get on your own. Though they won't attack you, you can still destroy a Tripper for some refills.

Jump on to its back and immediately roll into a ball and use the Morph Ball ability to safely pass under the spikes ahead.

When you come to a metal block on a pillar, jump from the Tripper onto the block. Work your way across the pillars -- jumping over the spikes and past the closing gate until you reach another Tripper.

Follow the same procedure until you reach a blue door.

This area is home to Multiviolas and a new enemy type, that resembles the Dragon seahorses you saw earlier. But these fire spitters walk on two legs.

These walking seahorses initially hide in the ground and leap out at you, before patrolling fiery areas. They attack by spitting fire.

Work you way to the very top, and ignore the doors to your right until you come across a blue door to your left.

Proceed through this door back into the green bubbly-like environment. You've visited this room earlier, but couldn't explore the right side of the bubble cave.

Follow this unexplored area upwards until you see a green door to you right. Avoid the Cacatac and exit through the door.

The next room has a bubble walkway across bubbling lava, with three Skree hanging from the ceiling.

Angle your shot and snipe them one by one. One of your shots is sure to break a ceiling block, revealing a passage upwards.

Refill your health using the Gamet spawn point, then exit through the right blue door.

You will enter a very long tunnel with block bridges that crumble when you step on them. There are also some Metaree and Garuta waiting to collide with you on the way. The solution is simple, hold B and dash through the entire room. Don't stop until you get to the far side of the room with a red door.

Stand two blocks away from the door and aim your beam upwards and fire. You will reveal a Missile Tank embedded in the bubble ceiling. Jump up to claim it.

Open the red door by firing five Missiles at it and enter.

Within this room there is a seated Chozo statue holding a glowing sphere. Shoot the sphere and approach to gain the Speed Booster .

The area will become unstable and the screen will start shaking. Exit the room and return the way you came -- but you have to hurry.

The lava level is rising, so use the Speed Booster by dashing with B to avoid damage. Exit through the blue door.

Bomb the hidden blocks in the next room to descend and keep following the path back you came in from.

When you are back in the large, green bubble-like area, shoot the Cacatac and jump to the ledge it was sitting on. Now drop down to the left.

You are now back at the start of this area. Head to the Save Room we visited earlier which will now show up as an 'S' on the radar.

Leave the save room and once again follow the Morphing Ball passage tha's situated between the two heads opposite and below the door you just exited.

When you exit the passage enter the blue door to the left.

In the next lava chamber, follow the path to the left -- ignoring the drop in the middle -- until you come to another blue door. Enter.

As soon as you enter this room, dash with B and use the Speed Boost to break through the wall. Continue to do so until you hit a blue door. Shoot and enter.

You have made it back to the earlier save room. Save your data and leave through the blue door to your left. You will enter a familiar room.

Use the platforms in the middle of the room to make your way up. Pass the yellow door (you'll ned a Power Bomb to open it) and go through the next (green) door on your left. If you've previously unlocked it, it'll be blue, of course.

You can finally get through here, thanks to your Speed Booster.

Enter this room and dash past all the barriers until you reach another blue door.

NOTE: Yes, the Sova crawling through a pipe in the ceiling is a giveaway that there's a secret up there. Don't waste time looking for it -- we'll get to it in a minute. Your dash has likely also revealed some destructible blocks on the floor. You'll need the Power Bombs to open this passage.

You will now enter an area filled with lava. Luckily, the Tripper creatures with platforms on their backs are also present. There's a new catch, however: they will sink from Samus's weight. So you need to move quickly.

Use them to safely make your way across to the other side of the room and exit through the blue door.

The next room is guarded by Fune heads on the left and Sova crawling through a narrow shaft on the right. You can take the Sova passage by bomb jumping up, but avoiding the Fune isn't that difficult and it's easier to enter that shaft from the top. Just carefully time your jumps and continue upwards over the alternating platforms. You can save your Super Missiles.

Once at the top, you'll see a blue door to you right -- leave it closed for now!

Instead, bomb the ground immediately in front of the hatch and fall -- In Morph-Ball form -- through the hole.

Stay against the wall as you fall so Samus will rest on a ledge. Now let Samus roll to the left off the block she is balancing in and maneuver her into the third opening to the right.

You will discover a small room with a blue door. Enter.

Congrats, you have found another crucial secret chamber. The seated Chozo Statue is holding a glowing sphere. Shoot the sphere to gain the Ice Beam.

While not required to complete the game, the Ice Beam is crucial weapon -- and tool -- that opens up new passages. Shoot smaller enemies to freeze them, then use them as platforms to get up higher or cross chasms.

Once you have the Ice Beam, leave the room the way you entered and fall to the very bottom of the Morph-Ball passage. You will now be back at the beginning of the alternating steel ledges. Make your way to the top -- you can now freeze the Fune -- and go through the blue door.

Samus now needs to head to the elevator back to Brinstar to gain the next power-up.

To get there, freeze the Boyons and Ripper in this small, lava-filled chamber. You likely haven't encountered Boyons before. Here's what they do.

For such small little hoppers, Boyons have a ridiculous amount of HP. But their main purpose, at least as far as Samus is concerned, is to be frozen and become temporary stepping stones.

Roll through the Morph Ball passage and exit to the right.

You'll break through three layers of brittle blocks and land on solid metal pipes below, above the Speed Booster corridor.

You can bomb two blocks here to drop down, but it's much faster to just stay up here, roll into a ball, and head through the pipe to the right. You'll encounter a Sova that you can easily bomb.

Drop down on the other side via a brittle block and exit through the blue door.
