articles.title: The Case of the Missing Pudding Walkthrough - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: “The Case of the Missing Pudding” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks once Pompompurin’s Mama and Papa have been made Permanent Residents in
articles.body:
“The Case of the Missing Pudding” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks once Pompompurin’s Mama and Papa have been made Permanent Residents in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . Visitors can be invited to stay on the island once their Friendship Level has reached 5 Stars.

How to Complete The Case of the Missing Pudding

Pompompurin’s Mama and Papa are naturally the family of Pompompurin . They can be invited to the island as long as there is a Visitor Cabin in Gemstone Mountain that is furnished to their preferences. After arriving on the island, complete Daily Quests to raise their Friendship Level by 1 Star. When they reach 5 Stars, they can be invited to stay on the island permanently, and “The Case of the Missing Pudding” will unlock.

To start the quest, travel to the Dessert Boat Mailbox in Gemstone Mountain and talk to Pompompurin’s Mama. She’ll ask if you've seen any puddings and explain that she’s been making puddings all day, but they keep vanishing!

Pompompurin’s Papa says he’s on the case and invites you to be his assistant. Start by interviewing suspects to find out some leads.

Talk to Pekkle first in Gemstone Mountain. He exclaims it couldn’t have been him who ate the dozen puddings. Which seems suspicious, but he mentions he happened to see them on the window. Taken off the suspect list, it’s time to move to the next friend.

Talk to Badtz-maru on the Seaside Resort Docks . He’s a bit too excited to be a suspect, but he admits that he wouldn’t really be the type to steal pudding, only pizza. Given how much he wants to be a suspect and asks if he’s being a good one, there’s no way he’s the suspect.

Talk to Kuromi in Spooky Swamp . She ponders the missing pudding and suggests the obvious: aliens and pudding zombies. Of course! How could we be so blind?! Then again, Kuromi suggests that maybe there could be one other person who should be questioned: Hangyodon and the Nuls. Maybe Kuromi didn’t know anything about the pudding case.

Return to Pompompurin’s Papa and Mama to update them on the case thus far. The leads have gone cold, and there just may not be an answer to this puzzling mystery… Pompompurin’s Mama says that Pompompurin will be disappointed and warns to break the news gently.

Pompompurin joins shortly after and asks what’s going on. Pompompurin’s Mama explains that the puddings have gone missing; however, Pompompurin doesn’t seem disappointed. In fact, he remembers those puddings and claims they were delicious. The case is solved! Turns out, it was Pompompurin all along who had eaten the puddings. As long as he’s happy, all is well.

The quest concludes, and now Pompompurin’s Papa and Pompompurin’s Mama can be invited out as Companions to adventure around Friendship Island.

articles.title: Cafe Cinnamon Unite Walkthrough - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: “Cafe Cinnamon Unite” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks once many Cafe Cinnamon characters have been made Permanent Residents in Hello Kitty Island
articles.body:
“Cafe Cinnamon Unite” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks once many Cafe Cinnamon characters have been made Permanent Residents in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . That list of pups includes: Azuki , Cappuccino , Chiffon , Espresso , Mocha , Coco , and Nuts . Other prerequisites to access this quest also include completing the following quests:

To start “Cafe Cinnamon Unite,” seek out Cinnamoroll . He had a wonderful time spending the day with the pups, but he admits to being concerned about Milk once again. Thus, it’s time for a group meeting! Follow Cinnamoroll to Cloud Island Plaza to meet up with the rest of the Cafe Cinnamon crew.

Once there, talk to Mocha to initiate the official Milk Search Party! Although everyone gathered to explore Cloud Island, now seems like the perfect time to do a widespread search for Milk. He should have already arrived, seeing as how he left before Coco and Nuts did, but there’s still no sign of him. The pups will scatter across Friendship Island to seek out clues about Milk’s whereabouts.

At Gemstone Mountain , Cappuccino, Coco, and Nuts are searching around some boulders for any signs of Milk. When moving the boulders doesn’t work, step in to break the rocks up with the Pickaxe, then talk to Cinnamoroll. The group concludes that Milk isn’t in Gemstone Mountain.

Next, head to Mount Hothead , where Azuki and Chiffon are mildly distracted by the Ziplines and the Pizza Oven . Zipping up and down the mountain is tiresome work and has left the girls a tad peckish. Maybe it’s time for a snack. Step up to the Pizza Oven and bake 3x Dessert Pizzas for everyone.

Dessert Pizza: 1x Flour (My Melody's Daily Gift) and 1x Candy Cloud (Cinnamoroll's Daily Gift) or 1x Sugarkelp (Keroppi's Daily Gift) or 1x Swampmallow (Spooky Swamp)

After a quick munch, the group decides that Milk is not in this area either. Cinnamoroll thanks them for their help, and now it’s off to the next area, Spooky Swamp.

Travel to Spooky Swamp to catch up with Espresso and Mocha. They haven’t seen any signs of Milk yet, but do have a theory. Since Milk likes Marshmallows, maybe gathering a bunch of Swampmallows will lead them to where he might be or lure him to the group. Gather 10x Swampmallows from the Swamp, then talk to Espresso.

After meeting up with everyone, there’s still no sign of Milk. Mocha suggests meeting up with everyone back at the Seaside Resort to conclude their search and come up with a new plan.

Once there, Mocha officially states that Milk is not on Friendship Island. But Cinnamoroll suggests that there is one more person they can ask to be sure before starting the next phase of searching for Milk. The Island Spirit knows everything there is to know about Friendship Island, so verify with her one last time by visiting the Heart of the Island in Rainbow Reef .

The Island Spirit is impressed by how many friends Cinnamoroll has and remarks on the strong bonds between all of them fondly. Cinnamoroll asks her for help, and after getting a good description of what Milk looks and feels like through Cafe Cinnamon’s bonds of friendship, she closes her eyes and tries to search for him one more time. However, the Island Spirit cannot pick up on Milk at all.

Cinnamoroll is in a bit of a panic, but The Island Spirit reassures him, saying that there is one more person she can ask for help. With that, the Quest concludes, gifting the player a Cinnamoroll Rug .

Continue the adventure to save Milk in the next Quest, " A Gift for Cinnamoroll ", which unlocks more Visitors to help aid in the search!

articles.title: Sprites List (Chapter 7 Season 4) - Fortnite Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Thought Sprite hunting was over with the end of Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 3? Think again - they're back in Override and are a major part of Chapter 7
articles.body:
Thought Sprite hunting was over with the end of Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 3? Think again - they're back in Override and are a major part of Chapter 7 Season 4. There are currently 162 Sprites to collect, each with its own ability that affects your gameplay. This IGN guide teaches you everything you need to know about Sprites in Fortnite CH7S4, including all variants, rarities, and effects, plus tips on how to extract them safely. Use our Sprites Checklist to track your collection!

All Sprites in Fortnite Override - Sprite Checklist

There are currently 162 Sprites in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4, including 27 base Sprites plus variants. Use our checklist below to track your exact progress toward collecting and Mastering them all:

Overshield Sprite Rare Grants Overshield, with more per level Overshield Sprite

Onigiri Sprite Rare Grants Overdrive after using a Consumable item, lasting longer per level Onigiri Sprite

Storm Scout Sprite Rare Grants the Overdrive effect after taking a certain amount of storm damage. At max level, it reveals future Storm Circles. Storm Scout Sprite

8-Bit Sprite Rare Gives you an 8-Bit Shotgun in your first chest and grants a score multiplier. 8-Bit Sprite

Bush Sprite Rare Puts a Bush on you after a duration. At level 5, you'll gain a Bush after eliminations. Bush Sprite

Adventure Sprite Rare Upgrades a random item in your inventory each time you level it up. Adventure Sprite

Jonesy Sprite Rare Slowly recovers some Health and Shield for a short duration after taking damage. Jonesy Sprite

Birthday Sprite Rare Gives you a chance to receive a piece of cake when opening chests. Birthday Sprite

Sonic Sprite Epic Increases Sprint speed Sonic Sprite

Tails Sprite Epic Allows you to hover for a short duration Tails Sprite

Shadow Sprite Epic Automatically reloads your weapons over time, even when unequipped Shadow Sprite

Pond Sprite Epic Grants you a Super Jump after jumping, with more charges gained over time. Super Jump strength increases with each level. Pond Sprite

Morgana Sprite Epic Increases effectiveness of healing items, which increases with each level. Morgana Sprite

Dumpster Dive Sprite Epic Buffs heals from food and gives you a chance to find food when jumping out of dumpsters and porta potties and opening containers, with better food chance with each level. Dumpster Dive Sprite

Killswitch Sprite Legendary Grants Hangtime effect with improved accuracy. Hangtime puts you into a midair, slow motion animation which improves your aim and removes weapon bloom. Killswitch Sprite

Jackrabbit Sprite Legendary Allows you to double-jump. Jackrabbit Sprite

X-Ray Sprite Legendary Periodically marks nearby enemies. Frequency and radius increases with each level. X-Ray Sprite

Blinky Sprite Legendary Grants you Cloak when you take damage, which increases with each level. Blinky Sprite

Crash Bandicoot Sprite Legendary Jump to trigger a whirlwind attack, which damages and knocks back enemies. Damage increases with each level. Crash Bandicoot Sprite

Vampire Sprite Legendary Heals you when you damage enemies. Amount healed increases per level. Vampire Sprite

The Deer Sprite Legendary Buffs melee damage, which increases per level. The Deer Sprite

Klombo Sprite Mythic Drops random items at each level. It can only be leveled up by using consumables that grant Health or Shield. Klombo Sprite

Spooky Dash Sprite Mythic Grants you a dash that lets you phase through objects and walls. Each level reduces cooldown. Spooky Dash Sprite

Crown Sprite Mythic Grants extra Crown Wins after winning a Victory Royale. It can only be leveled up by winning matches and new variants are also unlocked by mastering it. Crown Sprite

Mega Man Sprite Rare Allows you to slide around like Mega Man, with slide length increased per level Mega Man Sprite

One Wish Willow Sprite Mythic Extract other players equipped Sprites when eliminating them. Push everything away when damaged. Gets upset when removed and marks you on the map. One Wish Willow Sprite

Honey Sprite Epic Chance to spawn bees at the hit location upon dealing damage with a ranged weapon Honey Sprite

Like the previous season, most Sprites have Special variants with an additional effect. These variants are rarer than their base counterparts and therefore more desirable. Variants include:

Cheat Master : Allows you to press any button when inputting Cheat Codes.

Loot Hacker : Increases chance of spawning items from your Loot Hacks.

Bounty Hunter : Chance for a Sprite will drop when getting an elimination.

Trick or Treat : Chance for candy to drop when you open containers.

Following player feedback from Season 3, Epic Games has added the following Sprite quality-of-life changes in CH7S4:

It now indicates when you've collected a Sprite previously and shows the name of a Sprite when you're near it.

The button-hold time for summoning a Sprite has been reduced.

As far as we're aware, there are no Sprites that are currently in the game's files but that are still unreleased.

Epic Games has confirmed that some Sprites from Season 3 "may" return later on in Season 4, though have yet to reveal which ones. We'll update this guide once we know more.

Once a Sprite reaches level 5 and you extract it, it becomes Mastered. The more Sprites you Master, the more additional rewards you earn, including Portable Extractors, Sprite Dust, XP, and rare Sprite variants.

Here are all the Sprite Mastery rewards, plus checkmarks so you can track what you've unlocked so far:

How to Extract Sprites - Tips and Tricks

To add a Sprite to your collection, you must extract it. There are three ways to extract Sprites:

Win a match with a Sprite equipped or in your inventory

The easiest and safest way to extract is to use a Portable Extractor, accessed via the Gizmo wheel. This allows you to extract a Sprite wherever you are, meaning you don't need to visit an Extraction Site. You can get more Portable Extractors from certain Daily Quests, or from the Sprite Dust Services Terminal at an Extraction Site.

You can purchase one Portable Extractor per day from a Sprite Dust Services terminal. Because new Sprites are being added constantly and it's random which ones will appear in your match, we recommend carving out five minutes each day to log in and buy your daily Portable Extractor - that way, you always have one when you need it. If you do need to use an Extraction Site, calling the crate will alert nearby players while you wait for it to drop. The best way to combat this is to use an Extraction Accelerator Gizmo, which drops the crate almost instantly, meaning you don't have to run and hide.

You obtain these via certain Daily Quests, and you can get two by entering the "TakeYourHeart" Admin Panel code. When trying to Master a Sprite, it's safer to extract it every level or so, rather than trying to get it level 5 in a single match. There's nothing worse than having a level 4 Sprite and then getting eliminated before you have the chance to Master and extract it. When this happens, it'll reset back to level 1, meaning you need to start all over again.

This is particularly true for harder-to-Master Sprites such as Klombo, which only gain XP when using certain consumable items like Shield Potions and Flopper fish. The slow and steady approach works best; while more time-consuming, it's so much less risky.

Some Sprites can be obtained via Admin Panel codes! Head to our Fortnite Lobby Hack Codes and Rewards guide for the full list .

Need more help with Sprites? Check out these Override guides:

articles.title: Weapons List and Locations - Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Guide - IGN
articles.summary: With a plethora of putrid enemies to destroy on your path to killing Dracula, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse gives protagonist Rose plenty of tools for
articles.body:
With a plethora of putrid enemies to destroy on your path to killing Dracula, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse gives protagonist Rose plenty of tools for the job. Yes, there’s a whip, but for players hoping to try different combat styles, there is actually a wide selection of weapons, broken down into a few distinct categories. So for those hoping to find and unlock every weapon on offer, follow this full Armoury guide and then get back to slaying vampires with a shiny new tool of destruction.

Below you'll find locations for all the different Weapons in Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, divided up by weapon type. Each weapon type has four rarities, increasing damage by 25 each rarity to a maximum of 100, and each weapon type also has a particular moveset and mechanics unique to that type.

The Longsword is Rose Belmont's default weapon, and is available to her from the very start of the game.

Location: Paris Streets: Justice District Sewers

From the Paris Streets: Court of Justice, travel to the bottom right exit, just to the right of the red door. After entering the docks, drop down through the platform, and slide through the small entrance on the bottom left.

Travel left to the Justice District Sewers, and drop down again, before using Holy Light to drop through the stone.

Swing to the left, timing it so you are situated between the two blades as you swing.

On the other side of the two stone pillars, swing with your whip to activate a switch.

Then swing back to the two stone pillars while holding Holy Light, then release it to bounce off the solid stone pillars and rise up above.

Then, with the platform lowered, swing on the Whip hooks above to reach the chest in the top right part of the room.

Where to Find the Joyeuse: Directions Coming Soon!

Where to Find the Valmanway: Directions Coming Soon!

A one-handed sword combined with a shield. Allows Rose to block attacks.

Location: Holy Innocents Cemetery: Serpents' Lair

Where to Find the Rusted Harpe and Aegis:

After defeating Medusa at the Serpent’s Lair, move through the exit on the right, and you will find the Rusted Harpe and Aegis at the bottom of the steps.

Enter the Library: Condemned Shelves from the middle entrance on the left side of the room, and you will be confronted with a large globe surrounded by floating orbs.

Move to the right-hand side of the room, dispose of enemies, and use the right-hand ledge to jump up to the platform at the same level as the globe.

Bounce on the bottom four glowing orbs specifically - without touching the others - to reveal an additional, larger glowing orb above the globe.

Bounce directly upwards on this new orb to reveal a secret area.

Continue bouncing upwards on the orbs, then use Aerial Rush to dash to the left, and Holy Light to pass through the stones.

Through to the next orbs on the left, bounce up once again, land on the right-hand platform without using Holy Light to gain purchase, then launch left while holding Holy Light and again use Aerial Rush to dash across to the leftmost part of this passage.

Once through to the left side of the passage - directly above the candlestick - simply drop straight down to find the chest.

Required Abilities: Aerial Rush, Holy Light

A two-handed weapon that can reach farther than other weapons.

From the Holy Innocents' Cemetery, move to the left of the fountain and start to rise up the large staircase.

At the top of the staircase is a room with a switch; head inside and hit the switch to begin a battle with several enemies.

Defeat those enemies, and move to the right to see a newly revealed wall, allowing you to double jump and reach above this room.

Jump between the existing wall and the newly revealed wall to reach above the room.

From here, move left to unveil the chest.

Location: Clock Tower: Mechanic's Ascent

Brass Knuckles are close-combat weapons that deal increased damage the more you launch sustained attacks.

Location: Paris Streets: Sewer Reservoir

From the base of the Paris Streets' Tower, specifically the Guard Level, move to the right.

Continue left until you see a grate, and then press the jump button while holding Down to pass through the grate below Rose.

On this lower level, smash the statue on the left, then move right and slide to sneak through the hidden passage.

Then, head to the grate on the right-hand side and once again drop down.

Jump across the wooden platforms to reach the chest on the left-hand side of this large room.

Opening the chest will then bring up the walls around this room, and several enemies will attack. Defeat them to escape with the new Cestus weapon.

From the Mirror Room in the Main Hall: Archives, exit through the right-hand door.

Use the whip to attach to and enter the floating mirror just above the entrance you just passed through.

Jump diagonally up and right to reach the floating wooden platform, while avoiding the moving buzzsaws.

From the wooden platform, quickly whip to the right and enter this second painting before the wooden platform crumbles.

Fire Rose out from the painting to the candlelit platform to the right. This platform will not crumble.

Use the whip to enter the next painting, above the candlelit platform.

Fire Rose out of the painting diagonally to the right and upwards. Importantly, the painting is swaying slight from left to right, so make sure to fire Rose while the painting is at the left-most part of its journey, to avoid firing Rose into the buzzsaw.

Once over, quickly land on the crumbling wooden platform and then jump to your right to drop down to another platform situated below.

Avoiding the buzzsaws, drop down to the corridor below with the red carpet. Then, start moving to the right, and then drop through the grate just below the pink anchor point.

In the next room, move left, and drop through another grate. Then, move to the right.

Either avoiding the enemy with the lance, or killing them, clib the staircase and enter this new room on the right-hand side.

In this new room, drop through the grate in the center to reach the new red door, and then enter the door.

Upon reaching the other side of the red door, jump up to hit the switch above Rose.

Then, with the walls next to the chest now down, Rose can move to the right and open it.

The large two-handed Greatswords are incredibly slow, but pack a large hit and can be spun in the air or charged on ground for a follow-up strike.

Location: Paris Streets - Roof of the Tower

Where to Find Durandal: Directions Coming Soon!

Long dual swords can be used to quickly strike out with rapid spinning attacks, and can be chained after the first swing completes for a devestating follow-up blitz.

The classic Vampire Hunter weapon returns, featuring the ability to deploy long-ranged strikes in any directions, and deals the brunt of its damage at the tip of the weapon's strike!

articles.title: All DLC and Post-Launch Cosmetics and Gear - Ghost of Yotei Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Ghost of Yotei's Echoes of Sekigahara DLC, Most Wanted mode, and their accompanying updates collectively added over 150 new Cosmetics and Gear for you to
articles.body:
Ghost of Yotei 's Echoes of Sekigahara DLC , Most Wanted mode, and their accompanying updates collectively added over 150 new Cosmetics and Gear for you to find, collect and use. On this page of our Ghost of Yōtei guide, we'll document every single one of them, and help you find them all!

It's well worth highlighting that, with the exception of the Damascus Steel Finishes , collecting these Cosmetics will also unlock them for use in the Legends Mode !

While the addition of New Game + added the new Tier V upgrades to all weapons, the appearance of Wolf Blade, Dual Katana and Odachi's blades were the same as with Tier IV. That changed with the 2.002 update , adding a brand new finish with a grey, ripple-like effect, known as "damascus steel", which in real-life history were possibly made using wootz steel imported from Southern India as far back as 300 BC.

These tables compile all of the new Armors and Dyes. Do note that several of the armors from the base game have also got their own dyes!

Cost: 10 Ghost Flowers at the Mysterious Merchant

Soldier's Faith is a Sword Kit that's only available in the New Game + mode , available from the title screen after completing all Revenge quests . You can buy it from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, for 10 Ghost Flowers.

A discarded soul. A silver tongue. A loyal follower.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Howling Waters - Colorful Dye Grounds

Cost: 15 Flowers at the Colorful Dye Merchant

Silver Venom is a Sword Kit that's only available at the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

You can find his Dye House in the Howling Waters area in the northern part of the region, just south of the "R" in the "Howling Waters" label on the map screen. Unfortunately the area is occupied by the Vipers, so you'll need to clear them out before you can access his wares.

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this Sword Kit from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 15 Flowers.

General Tadaharu's Sword Kit. A deadly marksman, he refused to take aim for Lord Saito. Disarmed, his blade stung the same, but in the end, a slow death.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Moashoro River

How to get: Collect from the Pillar of the Fallen

The Aimed Ire Sword Kit can be found at a Pillar of the Fallen in the Moashoro River area, which is on the northeastern border of the Ashoro Foothills region. It'll be next to the eastern side of a Viper Storehouse, and is placed right on the road.

...or at least that's how it appears on the map screen. In actuality, the Pillar is overlooking a clearing within trees and rock formations, and is sitting on top of the highest formation. On the western side of it will be a square hole in the ground with a ladder sticking out of it: head down here and through the tunnel, then climb the handholds at the end to get up to the Pillar where this sword kit is.

Vagabond's Defence is a Sword Kit that's only available in the New Game + mode , available from the title screen after completing all Revenge quests . You can buy it from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, for 10 Ghost Flowers.

Taken from Snake Contender Umakichi, who claimed the strength of a bear but died like a pig.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Moashoro River - Umakichi's Grasp

How to get: Kill Umakichi the Bear Slayer

Demon's Strength is one of the cosmetic rewards for killing Umakichi the Bear Slayer , the boss you face at the end of Umakichi's Grasp in the Ashoro Foothills region.

You'll be directed here in the course of the " Ashoro Springs " Revenge quest, making this a semi-mandatory cosmetic!

Nagato won his sword from a drunken lord who "did nothing with it but cut the grass his pissed in". He believed he could do more--be more--with it. Tap to Reveal .

How to get: Complete the " Dream's End " Revenge quest

Nagato's Blade is a Sword Kit that's awarded for completing the " Dream's End " Revenge quest in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . After doing so, the Sword Kit will be awarded to you automatically.

Prerequisite: Start the " Munetaka the Horse Thief " Bounty

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Shrouded Claw - Butcher's Clearing

How to get: Kill the " Munetaka the Horse Thief " Bounty

Rider's Bond is the Sword Kit that's awarded for killing Munetaka the Horse Thief , who's located on the southeastern border of the Ashoro Foothills in the Shrouded Claw area.

The trick is that Munetaka's area is initially blocked by bushes, preventing you from getting in. You'll first have to talk to a settler at a camp to the west-northwest, who'll ask for your help locating his horse Tomo. Once you do that, you can enter the arena, kill Munetaka, and get the Sword Kit!

Lady Ono's Sword Kit. Known for an elegant wit and a scathing cut, Lord Saito appealed to her boiling rage. An eruption of blades. Before Mount Akan, a lady's blood flowed like lava.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Toshibetsu Falls

How to get: Loot off the Pillar of the Fallen

The Volcano's Wrath Sword Kit is found at Toshibetsu Falls, an area on the western border of the Ashoro Foothills. As the name implies, there's a waterfall here over the cliff: the Sword Kit is up the northern side of the waterfall, on top of a rock formation with a single red tree on it.

Unfortunately the bridge up to the Sword Kit has collapsed. You can get up by checking around the eastern side of the rock formation: here, use the branch, handholds and grapple log to ascend the side of the cliff to the Pillar.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Howling Waters - Makami's Sacred Grove

How to get: Acquire The Wolf's Chosen Armor

Makami's Judgement is a Sword Kit that's acquired during " The Wolf's Chosen " Myth quest in the Ashoro Foothills. The kit is automatically collected and applied when you pick up the titular Wolf's Chosen Armor during the quest.

Viper's Appetite is a Sword Kit that's only available at the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Nature's Persistence is an Odachi Kit that's only available at the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this Odachi Kit from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 15 Flowers.

Cost: 20 Flowers at the Colorful Dye Merchant

Nature's Persistence is a Kusarigama Kit that's only available at the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this Kusarigama Kit from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 15 Flowers.

The first time Nagato taught me the "proper" way to tie a bow string, I made sure it was too tight. When he drew it back, it hit him straight in the face. He laughed and demanded fish soup in retribution. The sound of his laugh... Still makes me hold my breath for a second.

Prerequisite: Complete the " Dream's End " Revenge quest.

Nagato's Hankyu is a Hankyu Kit that only becomes available after you complete the " Dream's End " Revenge quest in the Ashoro Foothills.

Once you've completed it, you can then buy it from Ran the Bowyer for 10 Flowers.

Location: Yotei Grasslands - Yotei's Shadow Inn

Flaming Raid is a Hankyu Kit available from Ran the Bowyer, who hangs out in the Yotei's Shadow Inn in the Yotei Grasslands. It'll cost you 10 Flowers to purchase.

Soaring Demon is a Hankyu Kit available from Ran the Bowyer, who hangs out in the Yotei's Shadow Inn in the Yotei Grasslands. It'll cost you 10 Flowers to purchase.

Eager Rage is a Hankyu Kit available from Ran the Bowyer, who hangs out in the Yotei's Shadow Inn in the Yotei Grasslands. It'll cost you 10 Flowers to purchase.

How to get: Progress " The Storm Breaks "

Vengeful Aim is the starting Tanegashima Kit, and thus it's available the moment you get the rifle. This happens during " The Storm Breaks " Revenge quest, so it's not technically new, however it wasn't until the Compete Edition updates that it got a name!

A weapon first wielded in recklessness, now used to defend those who follow its example.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Shari Fields - Ashoro Springs

How to get: Complete the " Lady Kitami " Bounty AND the " The Storm Breaks " Revenge quest, then collect from any Onyrō Gift Altar

Lady Kitami's Tanegashima can be unlocked for collection by completing the showcase Bounty in the Ashoro Foothills, "Lady Kitami", in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

After completing that quest, you can pick this up by visiting from the Ashoro Springs Onryō Gift Altar.

Prerequisite: Complete the " A Handsome Reward " Revenge quest

Cost: 1,200 Coin from Taro the Scavenger

Perk: Enemies killed by wolves have a chance to drop their weapon.

The Charm of the Disarming Wolf is an upgradable Major Onryō Charm that's exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its perk is for enemies killed by wolves to have a chance to drop their weapon; while this is most applicable to the Wolf that follows Atsu across Ezo, its true potential is unlocked once you get The Wolf's Chosen Armor, which allows Atsu to summon the Makami Wolves to attack enemies on the battlefield, to which this Charm also applies!

The Charm of Disarming Wolf only becomes available after completing " A Handsome Reward ", the opening Revenge quest of the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC. After you've done that, you can buy it from Taro the Scavenger for 1,200 Coin. If you need a guaranteed spot to find Taro, head for Dead Man’s Tree in Ohara Plains, which is in the western part of Tokachi Range.

To upgrade this Charm, you'll need to hit enemies with thrown Melee weapons or Bolas (bolas are the ball-and-chain weapons that some Viper enemies use to tie up the feet of the target together). Note the wording: killing is optional! The Spider Lily Armor is great for this because it increases the chance that enemies killed in a Standoff can drop throwable weapons (the Charm of Swift Reward also does this, but only by a minor amount). If you're in New Game + , the Charm of the Duelist helps as it allows all enemies to drop Bolas (as well as Massive Weapons).

The Disarm Counter skill is useful for getting throwable Melee weapons, as is the Onyrō's Strike that lets you instantly disarm an enemy, at the cost of 3 Spirit. Its upgraded version is also very good because it lets you disarm three enemies, but this is only unlocked after completing "The Storm Blade" Myth quest. Lastly, the Charm of Quick Retrieval is inessential but useful as it makes Atsu pick up a dropped weapon immediately after Disarming an enemy of it!

Cost: 12 Ghost Flowers at the Mysterious Merchant

Perk: Increase to the rate at which enemies drop their weapons. All enemies can drop Massive Weapons or Bolas.

The Charm of the Duelist is a Major Melee Charm only available in New Game + , whose unique perk is to increase the rate at which enemies drop their weapons. On top of this, it also allows all enemies to drop Massive Weapons and Bolas, which are normally exclusive to the Viper enemies in the Ashoro Foothills of the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC !

The Charm of the Duelist is exclusive to the New Game + mode. Once you’ve started it, you can buy it from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, for 12 Ghost Flowers.

Perk: Arrows no longer fall over long distances and can pierce armor. Increases Ranged damage.

The Charm of the Archer is a Major Ranged Charm only available in New Game + , which has two perks. First, arrows no longer fall over long distances, which makes aiming significantly easier. On top of that, Ranged damage is increased, so all-in-all this Charm makes the Hankyu bow more versatile, and decreases the need to use the Tanegashima.

The Charm of the Archer is exclusive to the New Game + mode. Once you’ve started it, you can buy it from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, for 12 Ghost Flowers.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Howling Waters - Hunter's Rest Shrine

Perk: Brutes have an increased chance to drop Massive Weapons

The Charm of Massive Arms is a Major Utility Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC , whose unique perk is to increase the chance Brutes have of dropping Massive Weapons. This is very useful not just for the Viper Brutes of the Ashoro Foothills, but in all areas of Ezo, as this Charm applies to all Brutes in the game!

You can get the Charm of Massive Arms by climbing up the Hunter's Rest Shrine. You can start this climb in the Howling Waters, an area in the northern part of the Ashoro Foothills.

This Charm is upgraded by killing Brutes who are wielding Massive Weapons, aka the Viper Brutes. There aren't too many of those in the Ashoro Foothills, so we recommend obtaining this Charm as early as possible to make upgrading it easier. If you haven't upgraded it yet, you'll have to unlock the ability to replay Occupied Locations and Boss Fights by completing the main story. Once you've done so, we suggest replaying the fight against Umakichi the Bear Slayer, as this fight has two Viper Brutes in it!

Perk: The wolf may save you from being detected while in stealth. Can only trigger once every 5 minutes.

The Charm of the Wolfpack is an upgradable Major Stealth Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its perk is for a chance that the wolf may save you from being detected while in stealth, or attack a ranged enemy who is targeting you. The Level III version of the Charm even applies this to enemies targeting you in combat! The catch is that it has a 5 minute cooldown, meaning it can only be used once unless your stealth run / combat sequence is particularly long.

The Charm of the Wolfpack only becomes available after completing " A Handsome Reward ", the opening Revenge quest of the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC. After you've done that, you can buy it from Taro the Scavenger for 1,000 Coin. If you need a guaranteed spot to find Taro, head for Dead Man’s Tree in Ohara Plains, which is in the western part of Tokachi Range.

To upgrade the Charm of the Wolfpack, you'll need to experience wolf interventions, which means the wolf needs to appear on her own rather than being directly summoned via The Song of the Wolf. Unlocking Wolf Techniques under the "Summon" tree helps, as they allow the wolf to appear when Atsu is downed, using Onryō's Howl, engaging a Standoff, or throwing something at an enemy. But the biggest aid is wearing The Wolf's Chosen Armor , which allows the wolf to appear by Atsu's side on her own before combat without using The Song of the Wolf, and it counts towards this Charm!

Perk: Smoke Bombs inflict Poison which deals minor Stagger damage over time. Minor increase to the time it takes for an enemy to detect you.

The Charm of the Unseen is a Major Stealth Charm that is exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . It has two perks: first, Smoke Bombs will inflict Poison that will deal minor Stagger damage over time, making Smoke Bombs a bit more useful for the enemies you can't Assassinate after using one. The second perk is a minor increase to the time it takes for an enemy to detect Atsu, similar to the Charm of Lingering Shadows.

The Charm of the Unseen is exclusive to the New Game + mode. Once you’ve started it, you can buy it from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, for 12 Ghost Flowers.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Viper Storehouse

Perk: Increase the maximum number of attacks with a Massive Weapon

The Charm of Smashing is a Minor Melee Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its unique perk is to increase the maximum number of attacks a Massive Weapon has. Note that this is for the weapons durability, so swinging but not hitting an enemy will not count as a hit!

The Charm of Smashing is awarded to you by liberating your first Viper Storehouse, which are small buildings hidden within a ring of trees in the Ashoro Foothills. Your first one involves meeting a settler trying to get in and reclaim the people's food: after helping him, he'll award you this Charm.

To upgrade this Charm, you need only liberate more Viper Storehouses. There are exactly enough Storehouses to fully upgrade this Charm, so completing the " Viper Storehouses " Tale quest will upgrade it to the maximum.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Shrouded Claw - Marshland Fox Den

Perk: Earn Spirit when catching an Arrow (requires Catch Arrow skill).

The Charm of Divine Grasp is an upgradable Minor Ranged Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its unique perk is for Atsu to earn Spirit whenever she successfully catches an arrow. Do note that this requires unlocking the Catch Arrow skill!

You get the Charm of Divine Grasp by completing the Marshland Fox Den. This can be found in Shrouded Claw, the southeastern area of the Ashoro Foothills region.

Upgrading this Charm involves catching Arrows with the Catch Arrow skill. So long as your game is updated, you'll have this skill available to purchase under Growth -> Onryō -> Ranged. To catch an arrow, press and hold the O button after an arrow has been fired, and Atsu will automatically catch it and fire it back at the shooter.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Moashoro River - Fortune's Asobiya

How to get: Complete the " A Mother's Love " Tale quest

Perk: Concentration regains faster the drunker you are

The Charm of Drunken Focus is a Minor Ranged Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its unique perk is for Concentration to regain faster the more drunk Atsu is. This is a rather niché application, so we only recommend using it if you've crafted a Drunk Loadout, which you can do with the following:

Charm of Drunken Adversary - Sake may drop from Standoff kills.

Charm of Abundant Drink - Increase Sake capacity by 1.

Charm of the Blind Drunk - Throwing Sake Jars will blind enemies.

Charm of the Drunken Brawler - Damage taken while drunk can be restored by damaging enemies.

You get the Charm of Drunken Focus by completing the " A Mother's Love " Tale quest. You do this at the Fortune's Asobiya gambling den in the Ashoro Foothills, which Atsu scopes out and adds to the map when she first arrives in the region and scopes it out with her spyglass.

Perk: Damage taken while Drunk can be restored by attacking enemies.

The Charm of the Drunken Brawler is a Minor Defence Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its perk is that damage taken while Drunk can be restored: the Restorable Health appears grey, and can be restored by damaging enemies. The one catch is that this DOES NOT stack with the Odachi's Unstoppable Force technique, meaning you cannot restore double the health by attacking with the Odachi.

This Charm is unlocked in a rather unique way. While exploring the Ashoro Foothills, you may encounter a camper who tries to flag Atsu over by asking for some food. Stop at his camp and oblige him by cooking any meal: he'll give you this Charm as thanks!

Perk: Poison effects deal more Stagger damage, last longer, and inflict damage to enemy Health.

The Charm of Enhanced Poison is a Minor Utility Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . It has several perks revolving around Poison: it deals more Stagger damage, lasts longer, and is able to inflict damage to enemy Health. This makes Poison much more useful, meaning this Charm should be the backbone of any Poison-based Loadouts.

The Charm of Enhanced Poison only becomes available after completing " A Handsome Reward ", the opening Revenge quest of the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC. After you've done that, you can buy it from Taro the Scavenger for 750 Coin. If you need a guaranteed spot to find Taro, head for Dead Man’s Tree in Ohara Plains, which is in the western part of Tokachi Range.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Blooming Trails - Riverside Fox Den

Perk: Throwing a Sake jar at an enemy makes them massively weaker to fire attacks for a short duration.

The Charm of Lord Adachi's Demise is a Minor Ranged Charm exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Its unique perk is that throwing a Sake Jar at an enemy makes them massively weaker to fire attacks for a short duration, making this a great choice for Loadouts focused around the use of fire.

The name of this Charm is actually a reference to the opening of Ghost of Tsushima! There, Lord Shimura has Lord Adachi, husband of Lady Masako, meet the mongols to challenge their finest warrior. Khotun Khan instead douses him in wine and lights him aflame with a torch, before beheading him.

You can get this Charm by completing the Riverside Fox Den, which you can find in Blooming Trails, an area on the western border of the Ashoro Foothills.

Perk: Detect nearby hidden enemies outside of combat without listening for them.

The Charm of Awareness is a Minor Utility Charm with a very unique perk. With it equipped, Atsu is able toe Detect nearby hidden enemies outside of combat without having to Listen for them first.

While this sounds incredibly useful, to the best of our testing this Charm doesn't actually work : it doesn't work when infiltrating Yōtei Six Camps, nor does it help detecting enemy ambushes from tall grass.

The Charm of Awareness only becomes available after completing " A Handsome Reward ", the opening Revenge quest of the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . After you've done that, you can buy it from Taro the Scavenger for 750 Coin. If you need a guaranteed spot to find Taro, head for Dead Man’s Tree in Ohara Plains, which is in the western part of Tokachi Range.

Prerequisite: Defeat Lord Saito in Most Wanted

How to get: Buy the Joy of the Stars Dye for 10 Boss Tokens

The Loyalty in the Stars Hat is exclusive to the Most Wanted mode, and references the Astro Bot games. To get it, you'll need to defeat Lord Saito in this mode, then buy the Joy of the Stars dye for the Onryō Armor, which costs 10 Boss Tokens from the Most Wanted Merchant.

This section houses all of the Hats and Helmets added for the Complete Edition's Echoes of Sekigahara and the Most Wanted Mode. Note that it also includes many Hats that DO NOT require the Complete Edition to access, as they were added in the 2.002 update available for everyone.

Prerequisite: Fully heal the Ashoro Foothills and restore Ashoro Springs

This headband is in a rather hidden location, because it doesn't become available until you meet a set of rather specific requirements. In particular, you'll need to all but fully heal the Ashoro Foothills, as well as two quests that help restore the Ashoro Springs. The quests that do this are:

After doing all of these, return to Ashoro Springs and look for a woman in white near the middle of town who you can talk to. She'll be near a large rock between the main Inn building and the Communal Cookhouse.

When you talk to her, she'll mention a fox named Momo who used to visit the town, but appears to have been driven off by the Vipers.

Face the large red tree, then check the hot spring to the left of it to find Momo the fox: interact with it, and Atsu will feel inspired to paint the town in a Sumi-e Painting. Complete it, and you'll receive this headband!

It's never too late to change the path you walk on.

Prerequisite: Progress " The Gentle Giant " Tale quest

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Blooming Trails

This headband is also a somewhat hidden Sumi-e Painting. To get it, you'll need to progress " The Gentle Giant " Tale quest, which you can start by finding the camp atop the river cliff east-southeast of Ashoro Springs.

After doing this, you can find the Tale's second part at the lowest wasterfall of the river directly west of Ashoro Springs. Here you can find a campsite to progress the quest: do so, and Atsu will paint a Sumi-e, unlocking this headband!

How to get: Buy the Champion of Democracy Dye for 10 Boss Tokens

This Helldivers II -referencing helm is unlocked in the Most Wanted mode. First, you'll need to defeat Lord Saito for the first time: after doing that, you can find the Champion of Democracy Dye available for 10 Boss Tokens: buy it to also unlock this helmet!

Issued to those serving the Western Army in the battle of Sekigahara.

How to get: Complete the " A Buried Promise " Revenge quest

The Western Army Hat is the hat for the Armor of the Western Army outfit. It's unlocked automatically by completing the " A Buried Promise " Revenge quest.

Owned by a gentle soul forced into a world of violence.

How to get: Complete " The Gentle Giant " Tale quest

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Akan Woodlands

Koroku's Hat is the reward for completing " The Gentle Giant " Tale quest, a quest we partially described above for the New Direction Headband. This hat is acquired by fully completing the Tale, which is done in the Akan Woodlands in the southern part of the Ashoro Foothills.

The Forest's Bounty Hat is a helm located near the Riverside Fox Den, located in the Blooming Trails area on the western border of the Ashoro Foothills.

From the Riverside Fox Den, head directly southwest towards a gravel slope heading into a small valley. At the bottom, squeeze through the gap on your left: on the other side, look right to spot a chest. Open it to get this hat!

Cost: 12 Flowers at the Colorful Dye Merchant

Koromodako's Folly is a hat that is exclusively available at the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills.

You can find his Dye House in the Howling Waters area in the northern part of the region, just south of the "R" in the "Howling Waters" label on the map screen. It'll initially be occupied by Vipers, so you may have to clear them out first.

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 10 Flowers.

Pre-requisite: Complete the " A Mother's Love " Tale quest

The Tracker's Straw Hat is the rare open-world Vanity Item that requires you to complete a different quest before it appears. You'll need to first complete the " A Mother's Love " Tale quest at Fortune's Asobiya, which Atsu scopes out with her spyglass when she first arrives in Ashoro Springs.

After completing this quest, head for the bottom of the cliff to find a woman who was thrown down there from the top. To the left of her is a chest: open it to get the hat!

The Sun Touched Straw Hat is a Complete Edition hat that's actually available to all players of Ghost of Yōtei: you can buy it for 10 Flowers at Taro the Scavenger. You can find his permanent spot at Dead Man’s Tree in Ohara Plains, on the western side of Tokachi Range.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Howling Waters

The Judgement's Path Hat is a Vanity Item that can be found in the open world, specifically the Ashoro Foothills, meaning it's exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

You can find it in the Howling Waters area at the northern end of the region. Here, check the north-eastern border (directly north of the "Waters" of the "Howling Waters label on the map screen) to find an overturned cart surrounded by some skeletons. This chest will be on the wheel of the cart.

Cost: 10 Flowers at the Colorful Dye Merchant

The Midnight Mukade Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Cost: 10 Ghost Flowers from the Mysterious Merchant

The Dawn Mukade Hat is one of the hats available from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, who is only accessible in New Game + . It will cost you 10 Ghost Flowers.

You can find Masujiro the Melodious right from the start of New Game +: his camp is one of the locations Atsu spots with her Spyglass immediately after the title card. He'll be in a cluster of trees directly between Atsu's Home and the Yotei's Shadow Inn.

The Ocean's Storm Straw Hat is one of the hats available from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, who is only accessible in New Game + . It will cost you 10 Ghost Flowers.

The Trapper's Straw Hat is one of the hats available from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, who is only accessible in New Game + . It will cost you 10 Ghost Flowers.

Cost: 5 Flowers at the Colorful Dye Merchant

The Trodden Straw Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 5 Flowers.

The Silent Straw Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Cost: 7 Flowers at the Colorful Dye Merchant

The Dark Gaze Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 7 Flowers.

Viewed kindly by the gods. A touch of inspiration.

The Heavenly Thoughts Hat is one of the hats available from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, who is only accessible in New Game + . It will cost you 10 Ghost Flowers.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Blooming Trails - Makami Bridge

The Floating Scale Hat can be found in the open wilds of the Ashoro Foothills, meaning it's exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

To the east-southeast of Ashoro Springs is the Makami Bridge, which spans over a river chasm. Use the handholds to climb down from the bridge to the river, then check under the southern end of the bridge for a chest with this hat inside.

Location: Yōtei Grasslands - Yōtei River - White Dye House

Cost: 7 Flowers at the White Dye Merchant

The Kindness in Death Hat is a hat that can only be purchased from the White Dye Merchant. You can find her in the Yōtei River area in the northwestern part of the Yōtei Grasslands.

Look for it on the southern side of the river, close to the Yōtei River Bamboo Strike. You can find the White Dye Merchant standing outside the main building. Talk to her and buy the helmet!

How to get: Complete the " Lady Kitami " Bounty

This helmet is one of the rewards for completing the " Lady Kitami " Bounty, which is unlocked by clearing two Ashoro Foothills Bounties (assuming at least one of them isn't related to the " Ashoro Springs " Revenge quest). After completing the Bounty, you'll automatically get this helmet!

A sanctuary for those seeking to rest their wings.

How to get: Free and follow the Golden Bird in the Ashoro Foothills

The Nature's Promise Helmet is found via rather unique means. While roaming the Ashoro Foothills, you may encounter a small Viper camp boasting about capturing the Golden Bird that's been helping Atsu locate points of interest throughout her adventures.

Defeat the Vipers, free the bird, then follow it to a tall dead tree with a package hanging from a rope. Cut the rope with one of your bows, then collect it to get this Helmet!

Taken from Snake Contender Bunzaemon, betrayed by his own men, left alive to pay for the slaughter he caused.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Blooming Trails - Nishimura Slaughterhouse

How to get: Complete the " Bunzaemon the Butcher " Bounty

The Butcher's Helmet is one of the rewards for completing the " Bunzaemon the Butcher " Bounty. This can be done by liberating the Nishimura Slaughterhouse on the western border of the map, directly north of the "Trails" in the "Blooming Trails" label on the map screen.

You'll get this helmet automatically for liberating the Nishimura Slaughterhouse by defeating Bunzaemon the Butcher and his men.

A helmet left behind from a land across the sea.

Prerequisite: Complete the " Another Man's Treasure " Revenge quest

The Foreign Helmet is a unique helmet from Portugal, which only appears after you've completed the " Another Man's Treasure " Revenge quest.

After you've done so, you'll unlock " A Past and Present Battle ". Head to its starting point in the Howling Waters area at the northeastern border of the map. Here, check to the right of the entry point to find a chest next to an abandoned cart: open it for the helmet!

If this chest isn't present, it's probably because you travelled here on foot. To fix this, fast travel to refresh the game world, spawning the chest.

Taken from Snake Contender Umakichi who claimed the strength of a bear but died like a pig.

How to get: Complete the " Umakichi the Bear Slayer " Bounty

This helmet is a reward for completing the " Umakichi the Bear Slayer " Bounty. This can be done by clearing out Umakichi's Grasp, a hunting ground at the northeastern end of Moashoro River on the northeastern border of the Ashoro Foothills.

You'll get the helmet automatically after clearing out the area and defeating Umakichi and his men.

Taken from Nobushige the Unbreakable. Heavy is the burden of war torn memories.

How to get: Complete the " Nobushige the Unbreakable " Bounty

This helmet is a reward for completing the " Nobushige the Unbreakable " Bounty. This is a multi-part Bounty that takes you all across the Ashoro Foothills, ending in a final duel at Toshibetsu Falls.

Read the page linked below to learn where to find Nobushige and how to defeat him.

How to get: Upgrade The Wolf's Chosen Armor to Level II.

The Mourning Helmet can be obtained by collecting The Wolf's Chosen Armor . This is obtained in the identically-named "The Wolf's Chosen" Myth quest, which you get mandatorily when Atsu scouts the Ashoro Foothills with her spyglass when first arriving.

Once you've done that, head for Ginju the Armorer to upgrade the armor to Level II. Ginji can be found at every Inn, or summoned directly to a fresh campsite via the Wolf Pack menu.

How to get: Upgrade the Wolf's Chosen Armor to Level IV.

The Howling Helmet can be obtained by collecting The Wolf's Chosen Armor, then upgrading it to Level IV at Ginji the Armorer. Ginji can be found at every Inn, or summoned directly to a fresh campsite via the Wolf Pack menu.

The Blind Judgement Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Location: Ishikari Plain - Stone Jaw Coast - Crimson Dye Beach

Cost: 5 Flowers at the Crimson Dye Merchant

The Bleeding Judgement Hat can be found at the Crimson Dye Merchant in Ishikari Plain. To find her, head for the Crimson Dye Beach on Stone Jaw Coast, located north-northwest of Ishikari Castle.

Here you’ll find the Crimson Dye Merchant’s workplace, but she’s currently out on her boat. To summon her, locate the campfire and light a fire there to draw her to shore.

The Eyes of Fire Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

How to get: Complete " The Nature of War " Revenge quest, then collect from any Onryō Gift Altar.

The Stag's Grace Hat is obtained by completing " The Nature of War " Revenge quest, then collecting it from any Onryō Gift Altar.

The Elegant Fortitude Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Cost: 7 Flowers at the Crimson Dye Merchant

The Crescent Blood can be found at the Crimson Dye Merchant in Ishikari Plain. To find her, head for the Crimson Dye Beach on Stone Jaw Coast, located north-northwest of Ishikari Castle.

Location: Oshima Coast - Otsuki River - Blue Dye House

Cost: 7 Flowers at the Blue Dye Merchant

The Crescent Mist Helmet is a Vanity Item you can get at the Blue Dye Merchant, located in Oshima Coast.

You can find her Dye House on Otsuki River upstream from the Oiso Fishing Village, where you can buy this for 7 Flowers.

A glimpse of treasure. A sunrise of gold.

The Gilded Crescent Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

The Crescent Death Helmet is a hat that can only be purchased from the White Dye Merchant. You can find her in the Yōtei River area in the northwestern part of the Yōtei Grasslands.

Prerequisite: Complete the " Bunzaemon the Butcher " Bounty quest

The Jade Skin Helmet is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . However, it doesn't appear in his stock until you first complete the "Bunzaemon the Butcher" Bounty quest at the Nishimura Slaughterhouse.

You can find the Colorful Dye House in the Howling Waters area in the northern part of the region, just south of the "R" in the "Howling Waters" label on the map screen. It'll initially be occupied by Vipers, so you may have to clear them out first.

Once the area has been liberated, you can buy this from the Colorful Dye Merchant for 12 Flowers.

The Akan's Embrace Helmet is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

The Quiet Perspective Hat is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Shrouded Claw

The Empty Promises Hat is a Vanity Item that can be found in the open wilds of the Ashoro Foothills. It is located in the Shrouded Claw area on the southeastern border of the region. Head for the southeastern end of the river that cuts through that area.

Here you'll come across a waterfall: check the base of the left-hand cliff to find a chest with this hat inside. There may also be a small camp here with a Bounty Poster for Munetaka the Horse Thief.

The Sun Touched Straw Hat is a Complete Edition hat that's actually available to all players of Ghost of Yōtei: you can buy it for 10 Flowers at Taro the Scavenger.

To those who create, to those who play, the sun rises on the stories lived.

Prerequisite: Complete the " Umakichi the Bear Slayer " Bounty

The final hat in the game can be found at Umakichi's Grasp, however you won't be able to access it until you complete the " Umakichi the Bear Slayer " Bounty.

After doing so, look for a bear cub in the middle lake area and follow it to a spot where you can yank down some rocks. Climb all the way to the river at the top.

Here, you'll find four totems representing some of Sucker Punch's past works. Bow to each one by swiping down on the touchpad, and you'll get this Headband!

The Charm of the Stars Mask is exclusive to the Most Wanted mode, and references the Astro Bot games. To get it, you'll need to defeat Lord Saito in this mode, then buy the Joy of the Stars dye for the Onryō Armor, which costs 10 Boss Tokens from the Most Wanted Merchant.

An heirloom that withstood impossible odds.

How to get: Unlock Jin Sakai in Most Wanted

The Stag Mask is also exclusive to the Most Wanted mode. To get it, you'll need to unlock Jin Sakai, which you can do by spending 28,000 Coin in the mode. While looking similar to the Ghost Mask, this is actually its predecessor from Jin's father, Kazumasa.

How to get: Complete " The Nature of War " Revenge quest, AND Complete the " Call of the Hunt " Revenge quest

Complete " The Nature of War " Revenge quest, AND

Complete the " Call of the Hunt " Revenge quest

The Fury Unbounded Mask is the only Onryō Mask that's exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC , but it has a double unlock behind it. To get it, you'll first need to complete both the final main quest of the DLC, " The Nature of War ", as well as the " Call of the Hunt " Revenge quest from the main game.

After doing both of these, you can pick this up from either the Blue Dye Merchant or the Colorful Dye Merchant .

This section houses all of the Masks added for the Complete Edition's Echoes of Sekigahara and the Most Wanted Mode. Note that it also includes many Masks that DO NOT require the Complete Edition to access, as they were added in the 2.002 update available for everyone.

The Western Army Mask is the mask for the Armor of the Western Army outfit. It's unlocked automatically by completing the " A Buried Promise " Revenge quest.

Saburo's handiwork. Used to hide one's identity and hunt down Imai the Faceless.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Akan Woodlands - Imai's Workshop

How to get: Begin the " Imai the Faceless " Bounty quest

The Fowl Game Mask is a mask that's given to you just for starting the " Imai the Faceless " Bounty quest. You can find it at Imai's Workshop, in the Akan Woodlands area at the southern end of the Ashoro Foothills. It'll be directly south of the gap in the "Akan Woodlands" label on the map screen.

Here will be a clearing where you can talk to Saburo the Mask Artisan, who you may remember from Ishikari Plain. Talk to him to begin the quest: after transitioning to night-time, you'll recieve this Mask!

Taken from Nobushige the Unbreakable, each piece a witness to a lost brother in arms.

This mask is a reward for completing the " Nobushige the Unbreakable " Bounty. This is a multi-part Bounty that takes you all across the Ashoro Foothills, ending in a final duel at Toshibetsu Falls. Read the page linked below to learn where to find Nobushige and how to defeat him.

A protector is born. Nature welcomes its kin.

The Mask of the Cub can be unlocked by collecting The Wolf's Chosen Armor . This is obtained in the identically-named " The Wolf's Chosen " Myth quest, which you get mandatorily when Atsu scouts the Ashoro Foothills with her spyglass when first arriving.

The Veiled Memories Mask is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Yotei Grasslands - Golden Foothills - The Road to Ishikari Plain

Ishikari Plain - Urara Forest - Oni’s Breath Inn

Once you’ve found him, peruse his wares to find and buy the Hidden Memories Mask.

If you missed him at The Road to Ishikari Plain, you can find him again at the Oni’s Breath Inn in Urara Forest, an area on the eastern side of Ishikari Plain.

The Stream of Thought Mask can be found in the open wilds of the Ashoro Foothills, meaning it's exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

To the east-southeast of Ashoro Springs is the Makami Bridge, which spans over a river chasm. Head for the northern end of the bridge, then go west along the edge of the cliff to find an abandoned camp. A chest will be here against a lot, with this mask inside.

The Trickster's Hour Mask is a mask that can only be acquired from Saburo the Mask Artisan, but in addition to that you must also by in New Game + for the mask to appear.

Once you've entered New Game +, you can find Saburo and his storefront at The Road to Ishikari Plain, a checkpoint gate in the Golden Foothills in the northwestern part of the Yotei Grasslands region. Peruse his wares to find and buy the Trickster's Hour Mask.

The A Thousand Faces Mask is a mask that can only be acquired from Saburo the Mask Artisan, but in addition to that you must also by in New Game + for the mask to appear.

Once you've entered New Game +, you can find Saburo and his storefront at The Road to Ishikari Plain, a checkpoint gate in the Golden Foothills in the northwestern part of the Yotei Grasslands region. Peruse his wares to find and buy the A Thousand Faces Mask.

The Deep Hunger Mask is one of the rewards for completing the " Viper Storehouses " Tale quest in the Ashoro Foothills. Once you finish it by liberating all four storehouses, you'll recieve this mask automatically!

The Crimson Thread Mask is a mask that can only be acquired from Saburo the Mask Artisan. You can find him and his storefront at The Road to Ishikari Plain, a checkpoint gate in the Golden Foothills in the northwestern part of the Yōtei Grasslands region.

Once you’ve found him, peruse his wares to find and buy the Crimson Thread Mask.

In summer, a few words by the riverbank.

Location: Ashoro Foothills - Howling Waters - Watchful Makami Altar

Unleash the pain of those who came before.

Once you’ve found him, peruse his wares to find and buy the Beautiful Rage Mask.

Deaf ears, arrogant eyes. Unmade, they lie still.

The Whisper in Death Mask is one of the items available from the Colorful Dye Merchant in the Ashoro Foothills, making it exclusive to the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC .

Cost: 7 Ghost Flowers from the Mysterious Merchant

Taken from an artisan whose handiwork emboldened a man's inner demons.

Once you’ve found him, peruse his wares to find and buy the River Tengu Mask.

For those of good intention and a hunter's code.

For those of bad intention and a murderer's cruelty.

The Mask of the Malicious is a Mask that only becomes available after you complete the " Dream's End " Revenge quest in the Echoes of Sekigahara DLC . Once you've done so, you can buy it for 200 Coin at Taro the Scavenger.

For those of ugly intention and a trickter's greed.

Once you've done so, you can pick up the mask from any Onryō Gift Altar in Ezo.

Taken from Ichizo the Toad. His final breath was for Yukiharu.

Prerequisite: Kill The Oni in Most Wanted

How to get: Buy The Oni's Armor for 3 Boss Tokens

The Oni's Gaze Mask is unlocked by killing The Oni in the Most Wanted mode. After doing so, buy The Oni's Armor for 3 Boss Tokens, which automatically unlocks this mask.

A smile and bated breath. An unexpected cut.

The Deadly Trick Mask is unlocked by killing The Kitsune in the Most Wanted mode. After doing so, buy the Robes of the Kitsune for 3 Boss Tokens, which automatically unlocks this mask.

A swift arrow in the dark. A blood moon rises.

The Midnight Trick Mask is unlocked by killing The Kitsune in the Most Wanted mode. After doing so, buy the Robes of the Kitsune for 3 Boss Tokens, which automatically unlocks this mask.

The Nine Tail's Shroud is unlocked by killing The Kitsune in the Most Wanted mode. After doing so, buy the Robes of the Kitsune for 3 Boss Tokens, which automatically unlocks this mask.

But Imai the Faceless did not miss Sakichi's eyes, vigilant of every mode, every expression, ready to spin a tale, to mold himself into a web of lies that would draw them in. But Imai reminded him that no one follows a leader with such clear disdain for the land and people that surrounded him. So he crafted Ukichi a Dragon's mask that would inspire devotion from the lowly peasants Ukichi so despised.

Looking towards the future, we must first gaze upon the past.

Cost: 15 Ghost Flowers from the Mysterious Merchant

The Onibi Keepr Mask is one of the masks available from the Mysterious Merchant, Masujiro the Melodious, who is only accessible in New Game + . It will cost you 15 Ghost Flowers.

articles.body:
Every guide at IGN is produced in collaboration by multiple passionate writers and video editors who thoroughly research, test, and edit their work. IGN's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Guide and associated videos are produced by the following staff and freelance experts.

This Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 wiki is a team effort, created with contributions from IGN staff members and freelance writers, including but not limited to:

Rory Norris - Guides Editor, QA Specialist

Angie is IGN's Weekend Guides Editor and has been playing Call of Duty for as long as she can remember, with her favorite games in the series being Black Ops 3 and Cold War. Having spent well over 40 hours in MW4's multiplayer so far, she can confidently say that her current favorite guns are the M4 and Oris 8.6 . With assistance from our contributing writers, Angie has helped cover guides across both multiplayer and DMZ, including our Best Settings for Modern Warfare 4 and Best Meta Guns in MW4 (Gun Tier List) .

Previously, Angie has spent the last year working on several other guides, including 007 First Light , Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Beta , Crimson Desert , Reanimal , and Disney Dreamlight Valley 's Honeyglow Woods Expansion . Some of Angie's other favorite guides she has worked on at IGN include God of War Ragnarok , Horizon Forbidden West , SCHiM , and Still Wakes the Deep , just to name a few.

Myles is a freelance writer who has worked with IGN for nearly three years, primarily in the commerce vertical. His first Call of Duty was the original Black Ops, and was an avid player of the series until about the time Call of Duty: Ghosts released in 2013. Since then, he's enjoyed the series from afar, and has returned for titles like Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, and Black Ops 7, with a specialty in the hardcore game modes and nostalgia for Capture the Flag.

When it comes to guides, Myles wrote Modern Warfare 4's entire campaign walkthrough, as well as character build guides for Avowed . But you can find most of his wiki and guide work on IGN's Magic: The Gathering page, of which he's the primary contributor.

articles.summary: Blackstone Fragments are found all over Phantom Blade 0. Similar to Sha-Chi Amber Fragments, Blackstone Fragments are another currency used to upgrade your
articles.body:
Blackstone Fragments are found all over Phantom Blade 0. Similar to Sha-Chi Amber Fragments, Blackstone Fragments are another currency used to upgrade your abilities on the skill tree. You'll need four Blackstone Fragments to create a full Blackstone, so be sure to stay on the lookout for as many as you can find. Below you'll find all of the Blackstone Fragments in Phantom Blade 0, but if you're looking for a specific zone, just click on the name below to go right there.

Weeping Creek Valley Blackstone Fragment 1

Upon entering the Outpost you'll see a locked gate to your left. In order to access this room you'll need the Cell key , which you can get by exploring the house to the right of the Outpost Bell. Go up the stairs and drop out of the backside of the house.

You'll notice a glowing orange piece of loot on the ground, which is the Cell Key. Grab it and head back to the locked door to find the first Blackstone Fragment in Weeping Creek.

Weeping Creek Valley Blackstone Fragment 2

You'll get the next Blackstone Fragment from defeating a group of enemies just shy of the Sha-Chi Tower bridge. This is also the same spot you'll go to for the Purge the Sect Tale to grab the bow. Upon defeating all of the enemies in this area, you'll be granted the Blackstone Fragment.

Weeping Creek Valley Blackstone Fragment 3

Go right past the Long Pillar Overlook Bell, across the wooden bridge, and through the small little housing cluster with a few enemies. In the back right of the area, you'll see a waterfall and some enemies. Dispatch them and claim the purple glowing chest to find the second Blackstone Fragment inside.

Weeping Creek Valley Blackstone Fragment 4

From the Long Pillar Overlook, head left toward the Sha-Chi Tower. You'll be able to head in from the ground floor. Go straight, and on your right-hand side you'll see a Furnace bomb; instead, head left and fight the two enemies in your path. Follow the stairs up into the lower floor of the Sha-Chi Tower. You'll be faced with multiple Bronze Men you'll need to defeat. Once defeated, you'll be given the final Blackstone Fragment in Weeping Creek Valley.

Now you're ready to move on to the Crimson Forest for your next batch of Blackstone Fragments.

This page is still being worked on, and more will be updated soon.
