articles.title: HomePod Mini 2 first look: Three things I love and one disappointment
articles.summary: The new Mini is faster, quieter, and gorgeous in green, but its upgraded Mac speaker feature didn’t work for me.
articles.body: When I first heard about the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 at Apple’s Welcome Home event last month, I was disappointed. It’s been six years since Apple launched its entry-level smart speaker, and all it got in the second gen was a chip bump, some color glowy stuff, and better AirPlay? For $50 more than the original, which launched at $99, Apple didn’t even upgrade the sound system. It felt like the company phoned this one in. Now that I’ve got my hands on a couple and set them up in my home office, I’m more enthused. The Mini 2 is so much faster than the first-gen Mini, playing music in a few seconds and responding to smart home commands just as quickly. If you’re fed up with standing over your HomePod waiting for it to finally do what you asked, then that alone is worth the upgrade. Here are my three favorite features of the new Mini 2 after spending a couple days with it, and my one big disappointment. [Image: Siri is much snappier and much less chatty The biggest upgrade for the Mini 2 is Siri AI, but that isn’t available yet. Apple says it’s coming “later” in a software update. However, the basic smart voice assistant has definitely improved. Siri on the Mini 2 is much snappier than on the first-gen Mini, regularly responding in under three seconds. This is thanks to a newer, faster processor (the S10, up from the S5) and Wi-Fi 6E support (up from Wi-Fi 4). When I asked Siri to play Taylor Swift, a song started in a couple of seconds. It correctly told me who won this year’s World Series in under two seconds, and turned off the light or opened the shades in under three seconds. [Video: HomePod Mini2 vs Mini 1 smart home speed] That’s a huge improvement over the up to 10 seconds I often have to wait for Siri to get things done on the first-gen Mini. However, asking something harder, like who will win the US midterm elections, still brings up the familiar offer to look at some web results on my iPhone. As I said, Siri AI isn’t here yet. The other new behavior I am really enjoying is that when I ask Siri to perform a smart home action, such as open the shades or turn on the lights, instead of “OK, Jen,” or “One sec,” followed by a wordy confirmation of the action that I often get on the first-gen Mini, the Mini 2 just does it and doesn’t talk back. It’s not silent for every action, but it’s quiet enough to be a noticeable improvement. [Image: This Mini is gorgeous in green and sounds great The green color is divine. This is the prettiest small smart speaker I’ve seen — and I’ve tried them all. Yes, Amazon’s Echo Dot Max’s purple is fun, the Google Home Speaker’s pale green is elegant, but Apple’s deep green is seriously sophisticated. It’s a color that fits in really well in various places around my home, and I’m so glad the company finally released a green option. It’s a big improvement over the slightly garish yellow and orange of the prior-gen Minis and the best of the new colors. [Image: [Image: I saw all the colors in person at Apple’s Welcome Home event, and while the pink is pretty, it’s very pale, and the blue is functionally identical to the first-gen blue, maybe a shade lighter. While a lot of folks will be happy with black (don’t get white unless you plan to dust it regularly), the green is my new go-to. [Video: HomePod Mini 2 vs Mini 1 Sound Test] Two green HomePod Mini 2s look so good on the walnut Nanoleaf monitor stand I’m testing; it’s like my office got an instant upgrade. And while Apple didn’t update the speakers in the Mini 2, it’s still a very good speaker for its size, doing a fine job with Bad Bunny’s bass and delivering clear mids and vocals. While $300 is steep for computer speakers, two as a stereo pair in my office definitely delivered on room-filling sound. You can finally disable touch A few weeks ago I fumbled for my phone on my nightstand and accidentally hit the top of my HomePod Mini, blaring music in the bedroom at 3AM. My husband was not happy. [Image: [Image: A new setting in the Home app now lets you lock the Mini’s top controls. This goes for all HomePods, old and new, and it’s a major quality-of-life upgrade. How often do you intentionally touch the top of your HomePod? I bet far less often than accidentally! The other new trick for the top of the HomePod is Sound Glow. This makes the LEDs display colors that match the album art of the song you’re playing (it’s also backward compatible with the first-gen Mini and the second-gen HomePod). It’s neat, but only works with Apple Music and Podcasts and is so subtle that I don’t feel it adds much to my music-listening experience. [Image: A stereo pair of Minis sounds very good. Here they’re pictured on Nanoleaf’s new monitor stand, which has built-in LED lighting. Signature feature fail Beyond the speed improvement, the other new feature I was excited about is the HomePod Mini 2’s ability to be the default speaker for your Mac using what Apple calls “a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection.” This creates a wireless point-to-point connection between the computer and the HomePod. You can pair a single speaker or a stereo pair to your Mac, and the feature also works with the second-gen HomePod. (Two or four HomePod Mini 2s can also now be part of a surround sound setup using the new Apple TV 4K.) Disappointingly, I couldn’t get the Mac speaker set up to work. I have the required hardware: a Mac that supports Wi-Fi 6E, running the public release of macOS 27.2 (a Mac Mini M4), and HomePods on HomePod Software 27.2. But the Sound pane in my Mac’s settings didn’t offer an option to set a HomePod via AirPlay as the default sound output. [Product: Apple HomePod Mini 2 | The Mini showed up and connected like any other AirPlay speaker, with the same flaws as regular AirPlay — occasional artifacting, drop-offs, and some lag with notification sounds — along with the Mac defaulting to its built-in speakers when the computer restarts, or anytime I activate Siri on the HomePod. I also tried with a stereo pair of Minis, but they also played over regular AirPlay. According to a 9to5Mac’s hands-on, when the persistent AirPlay is enabled, the HomePod Mini should show up as a default system output device in the System Information, and there should be an option to enable it under “Play sound effects through” in the Sound pane in System Settings, but neither was there for me. I have seen other reports of the same issue. I tried resetting both HomePods completely after they updated to 27.2 out of the box (I was on the HomePod Software betas, but 27.2 is now in general release), and the feature still isn’t working. I reached out to Apple, but the company hasn’t responded to my requests yet; I’ll update this article if I hear back or find a solution. [Image: There’s more to come I’ve only been testing the Mini 2 for two days, and while the real test will come when it gets its Siri AI upgrade, the chip bump and speed improvements make this a bigger upgrade than it initially seemed. Apple does need to work on the Mac pairing feature; it has a lot of potential, but based on my struggles here, it feels unfinished. I plan to do a full review once Siri AI launches, and of course compare it to Apple’s big new smart home release: the upcoming $299 Apple HomeView smart display. It is also a Home hub, but the screen gives it more functionality. At $149, though, the Mini 2 is now the cheapest way to get an Apple Home hub with Thread and Matter support.

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal Swap Places for Halloween With Mister Fantastic and Doctor Doom Costumes
articles.summary: Halloween had no shortage of viral costumes, but Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal might have taken the crown by swapping places as Mister Fantastic and Doctor Doom.
articles.body:
Halloween had no shortage of viral costumes, but Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal might have taken the crown by swapping places as Mister Fantastic and Doctor Doom.

Downey Jr. set Marvel feeds on fire late last night when he posted video of him and Pascal sharing their night dressed as their characters in next month's Avengers: Doomsday . Instead of playing Victor von Doom, though, he dressed up in Reed Richards' retro-themed blue outfit, with Pascal dropping his superhero attire to sport Doom's iconic metal mask.

It looks like Downey put a bit more effort into his Halloween costume, considering Pascal is wearing jeans and a sweatshirt, but the effect is still there. Finding a convincing replacement for Doctor Doom's magical get-up probably would have been more trouble than it's worth anyway. You can see Downey's video below.

They're the variants no one expected to see, but still the ones they got this Halloween. With Doomsday now just weeks away, we'll likely only see its many, many stars taking to social media to spread the word.

That said, this was a tiny bit more than a cute marketing stunt. While it was fun to see the two team up for a quick costume swap, Downey and Pascal still took the time to hit the streets and greet trick-or-treaters. Pascal shared a video of him and the Doctor Doom actor out on the town, walking amongst the crowd, on his Instagram story .

If that wasn't evidence enough, X/Twitter user Patrick Oneill shared pictures of him and two children greeting them in full Star Wars attire. With one kid dressed up as Pascal's character, the Mandalorian, Downey reportedly made a joke about the encounter by inviting them to come meet the "real" Mandalorian.

Avengers: Doomsday premieres December 18, 2026. When it marks the beginning of the end for this chapter of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, it will feature a cameo from Project Hail Mary's Sandra Hüller . It will also mark the final on-screen appearance of Sir Patrick Stewart . For more, you can check out how one recent poster highlighted Doctor Doom and his three Latverian witches .

articles.title: Taika Waititi Blasts Critics as 'Irrelevant, Out of Touch, Obsolete' Following Klara and the Sun's Negative Reviews
articles.summary: Marvel filmmaker Taika Waititi has called critics "sad lost souls who couldn't achieve their dreams" after his latest film, Klara and the Sun, premiered with negative reviews.
articles.body:
Marvel filmmaker Taika Waititi has called critics "sad lost souls who couldn't achieve their dreams" after his latest film, Klara and the Sun , premiered with negative reviews.

The director behind projects like Jojo Rabbit and Thor: Love and Thunder unleashed his true feelings in a post on Instagram . Tied to an image shared by ScreenRant earlier this week that reflects audience reception to the live-action book adaptation, Waititi posted an emoji-filled message taking aim at the reviewers who walked away from his new movie unimpressed.

"I haven't read a review of anything aimed at me or my peers in almost 15 years," he said, along with a series of emojis. "But I do listen to the people."

Klara and the Sun's critical reception has struggled in the wake of its October 23, 2026, release date. While Rotten Tomatoes has recorded mostly positive reactions from viewers at 74% favorability, its Tomatometer has sunk to a 'rotten' 26%. Its IMDb Metascore is similarly dire at a negative 30 out of 100 after 27 reviews. IGN did not review the movie.

Waititi said he's strayed from reading reviews for years, but that didn't stop him from pointing his 2.8 million Instagram followers to those who didn't enjoy the story his Klara and the Sun was trying to tell.

"So, this Halloween, let's spare a thought for those sad lost souls who couldn't achieve their dreams of becoming artists, and thus settled, and became critics. The same people who also hated Jojo Rabbit," he added with a laughing-crying-face and shrug emoji.

Jojo Rabbit is Waititi's 2019 project and his first since turning heads with Thor: Ragnarok in 2017. The writer, director, actor, and producer suggested critics weren't fond of the World War II-era dark comedy, though what negative reaction he's referring to here isn't quite clear.

Jojo Rabbit boasts an impressive 81% critical rating on Rotten Tomatoes . Although its IMDb score isn't quite as high at a middling 58, some of the reviews listed there are extremely positive, including an A- from Entertainment Weekly and an 85 from The Wrap . IGN gave the film an 8.5/10 .

"Klara and the Sun introduces audiences to Klara (Jenna Ortega), an Artificial Friend who wants nothing more than to find the perfect home," an official description for the film from Sony Pictures said. "When Klara meets Josie (Mia Tharia), each immediately senses a kindred spirit in the other. Josie has a fraught relationship with her mother (Amy Adams) and they’ve suffered great loss, but Klara’s innocent wonder and unwavering loyalty begin to heal the family and bring light to Josie’s complicated world."

While Waititi has had much to say about how critics have responded to Klara and the Sun, the films seems to have struggled to grab the attention of the average moviegoer, even if those who have seen it generally had a decent experience. According to Box Office Mojo , the movie adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro's novel of the same name has only managed to pull in a dismal 1.7 million worldwide after two weekends in theaters.

Klara and the Sun was also expected to debut in around 2,000 theaters last week before Sony seemingly rolled back that plan with an 800-theater debut, per Collider . Deadline reported that the company chose to stop reporting box office earnings for the film this weekend, too, with its budget reportedly set somewhere around $20 million - $40 million.

Waititi signed off his Instagram post, saying, "Irrelevant. Out of touch. Obsolete. In the bin." He added a trash can emoji, a crying face emoji, and a heart hands emoji.

Waititi was previously set to helm a Star Wars movie , but after six years of attempting to get the film off the ground, he announced the project was "on ice" earlier this month. He once said his take on the universe was trying to "harness a little bit more of the fun from" the original trilogy . What's next for Klara and the Sun remains unclear.

Fortnite is making almost everything in the Item Shop free for players for 14 days during the Treasure Hunters mini season - no, we're not kidding. There is a catch, though: you need to find and unlock Pirate Shop Access to do so, and it is extremely rare. This IGN guide explains how to access the Pirate Shop in Fortnite so you can plunder it and get cosmetics like the One Piece skins, emotes, and more completely free without spending a single cent.

How to Unlock Pirate Shop Access in Fortnite

To unlock Pirate Shop Access and get Item Shop items for free in Fortnite, you must find a Pirate Shop Access Token during the Treasure Hunters mini season. It is a random drop when opening chests , and has an extremely rare drop rate - at the time of writing, we've only seen a handful of people with it.

Once you find a token, you won't miss it as a large "YOU FOUND PIRATE SHOP ACCESS" banner appears at the top of your screen, as shown in a screenshot taken from @snowslept's gameplay below.

If you're in a team, your teammates also unlock Pirate Shop Access, too!

How Pirate Shop Access Works in Fortnite

When you return to the lobby after the match is over, a screen appears, informing you that you've unlocked Pirate Shop Access. You get two tokens, meaning not only can you get unlimited free Item Shop items during the Treasure Hunters mini season, but also once more in 2027. They both last for two weeks each, allowing you to claim almost anything from the Fortnite Item Shop for 14 days, potentially giving you hundreds of dollars worth of free stuff.

The first token can be redeemed any time between November 1 and December 15, 2026 . This means that, if you find one, you can claim the One Piece collaboration skins for free. They typically cost 1,600 to 1,800 V-Bucks each.

It's not just skins, though - almost anything requires V-Bucks is yours for the taking, including emotes, Jam Tracks, and other cosmetics. Paid items, such as bundles that cost real currency rather than V-Bucks, are not included. You can buy Sidekicks you don't own, but only once.

To activate your Pirate Shop Access token, open the Fortnite Item Shop and you should see a "PLUNDER THE SHOP" banner in the bottom-left corner.

Click this (hold Right Stick Click on PlayStation, Right Stick Click on Xbox, Right Stick Click on Nintendo Switch) and a banner confirming you want to "START YOUR PLUNDERING!" appears. Click "ACTIVATE NOW" to start your 14-day window of free items.

If an item can be claimed, you'll see "FREE" next to it. Go to buy it like you would a typical purchase from the shop, but instead of having to front V-Bucks to get it, it's just added to your library for free. Heck yeah!

Note that free items are only for you - you cannot gift them to anyone else.

articles.title: Heat Director Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidentally Shooting Himself in the Leg
articles.summary: Heat director Michael Mann was hospitalized with minor injuries after accidentally shooting himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range on Halloween.
articles.body:
Heat director Michael Mann was hospitalized with minor injuries after accidentally shooting himself in the leg at a Los Angeles gun range on Halloween.

TMZ confirmed the news with local authorities and the filmmaker's representative today. Mann was reportedly sent to the hospital for treatment and is in the process of being released.

"On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann," his representative said this morning. "He was treated and is being released."

Mann is known for his role in developing some of the biggest crime dramas of the last 40 years and, as noted by TMZ, is a highly experienced target shooter himself. The site described the incident as having occurred during a training exercise of some kind, with its sources saying the 83-year-old director had no intention of harming himself. Additional details are unclear.

An ambulance ride to the hospital is probably not how Mann wanted to spend his Halloween in Los Angeles. While the accident took a bite out of his weekend, the filmmaker is currently putting the pieces of his long-awaited Heat follow-up together behind the scenes.

Our first big confirmation that the ball was rolling for Heat 2 arrived in February of this year when The Dark Knight star Christian Bale confirmed he was set to start filming the movie in Chicago soon. Inception's Leonardo DiCaprio boarded the project in July, with both he and Bale then reportedly said to play Chris Shiherlis and Vincent Hanna, respectively. Filming was expected to begin in November, this month, at the time.

Mann is also responsible for movies like Ferrari, Public Enemies, and Manhunter. Also expected to appear in Heat 2 are Adolescence's Stephen Graham and The Bear's Ebon Moss-Bachrach . Story details about the follow-up aren't completely clear, though we do know that it will have Mann's novel of the same name to lean on .

While we wait to hear more from Mann, you can check out IGN's 8/10 review of Heat's Blu-ray release. You can also read our 7/10 review of Ferrari.

articles.body:
Alchemic Wisdom is a main quest in Enshrouded that sends you in search of two parts of a special collection of alchemical formulae. It’s an essential quest to unlock more concoctions from the Alchemist. This walkthrough will show you where to find the two pieces you need and how to combine them to advance Balthazar’s repertoire.

For tips on how to have the best experience in Enshrouded, check out the following pages:

To start Alchemic Wisdom, you must first complete Scientific Instruments For A Laboratory . Then, after you enter the Albaneve Summits, visit the Alchemist and ask him about “A New Frontier in Alchemy.” He’ll mention that he’s reached the limits of his skills and sends you on this quest to find valuable research to continue his studies

To complete Alchemic Wisdom, you need to collect two halves of the Ripped Alchemist’s Wall Hanging. The first is in a tower near the ruined town of Wickmouth in the Albaneve Summits. It’s southeast of the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire, and there are two neat points of interest you can easily hit along the way: a Flame Shrine and a Shroud Root. Just glide south from the spire to the Flame Shrine, then east to the Shroud Root , and you’ll still have plenty of elevation to glide directly to the tower.

Open the front door at the base of the tower on the southside and climb the stairs to the top . Use a Lockpick to open a door into the study at the top of the tower and look for the first wall hanging on the wall. Collect it to advance the quest.

Before you leave, look to the south side of the study to find a ruined bookshelf up against the wall. Break it down to access a small balcony on the other side with a gold chest. Then, fast travel back to the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire to set yourself to go after the other half of the wall hanging.

The second wall hanging is in a vulture nest in the Camellia Lake Marble Quarry west of the Albaneve Summits Ancient Spire. You can glide directly to it from the top of the spire . The nest you’re looking for is on the upper level of the quarry on the far west side .

Once you have both halves of the wall hanging, bring them back to your settlement and visit the Alchemist. Build an Alchemist Showcase and put it up somewhere in your settlement . Fill it with both halves of the wall hanging and you’ll complete the quest, earning you 350 XP in the process.

articles.title: Detour through Crateria - Super Metroid Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Once you've got the Power Bombs, you can take a detour through Crateria and Brinstar to mop up some helpful
articles.body:
Once you've got the Power Bombs, you can take a detour through Crateria and Brinstar to mop up some helpful upgrades.

Leave the room with the Chozo Statue where you got the Power Bombs to head back to the vertical shaft to the right.

Stop at the save room and then go to the remaining green door, toward the top. Unlock it with a Super Missile.

This room has a walkway over a thorny floor with Yapping Maws, a thorned ceiling, and three Side Hoppers who immediately come after you. Use your Charge (Ice) Beam to take them down. This will unlock the gray door to the right.

Roll over to the left side and drop a Power Bomb. Most of the metal walkway will be blown up.

The flower to your immediate right is actually not alive. You can drop through it to a hidden room below the floor.

Pick up the Power Bomb Expansion from the pedestal in the lower left corner.

Jump back up and use the metal blocks to jump over the Yapping Maw back onto solid ground (ie, the part of the walkway that wasn't blown up), and exit the room.

Climb the shaft and take the east elevator up to Crateria.

Now that you've got a few Power Bombs, you can open the way up here. Roll up into a ball and drop a Power Bomb to open the yellow hatch.

Climb the vertical cave, dispatching of the Sciser crabs you encounter on the way.

Sciser is a slow-moving crab alien that is found in multiple areas. While its stats are always the same, its colors differ depending on the environment. Scisers are weak to the Grappling Beam.

There is a double row of destructible blocks you need to shoot at the top.

You're now in the Crateria overworld again. There's a path to the right, via a yellow door, you shouldn't yet take. Instead, head left, blasting the Kihunters on the way.

Open the blue door and go through the glass pipe tunnel to the left.

You'll find yourself in the clearing where you landed your ship. There's a wall in the way that you could bomb, but it's a much better idea to build up your Speed Booster. Are you up for a challenge?

Since the runway is too short, start on the right side of the glass pipe, fire your blaster to open the door, then hold B and run to the left.

Keeping running! Samus will start flashing blue and purple, indicating that her Speed Booster is active. Smash through the wall and you'll get back to your ship.

With the Speed Booster active and Samus flashing, sprint just past the ship, then hit and briefly hold D-pad Down . This will store the Speed Booster energy in Samus's suit, to be unleashed at the press of a button. Samus is flashing orange and you now have three seconds to turn the energy into a Shine Spark, which will let Samus rocket through the air with the same destructive force as the Speed Boster.

In this case, we want to do the Shine Spark diagonally to the top left.

To do this the easy way, hold the right shoulder button, R , which makes Samus aim diagonally, face left and hit jump ( A ).

Samus will blast through the air and smash into the left rock wall, breaking the blocks there.

You can use regular bombs or a Power Bomb to clear a horizontal tunnel to the left.

Go through this tunnel and open the blue door to the left.

This room has a rising and lowering acid pool that will damage Samus when she attempts to cross. To make things worse, Yapping Maws (that cannot be destroyed) try to pull her into the acid.

To start, roll into a ball at the edge and drop a Power Bomb.

This blows up the destructible blocks hanging from the ceiling, and another one in the middle. These blocks can be destroyed with normal bombs, too, but you have to pick your battles.

What follows is an obstacle course that can be completed much more easily later in the game, so if you're struggling with it, just make a note to come back later.

You'll have to make your way to the left side of the cave, using frozen Wavers as platforms to avoid the rising acid, then dropping bombs to destroy the blocks in your way. Freeze any Maws in your way on the ground to get past them ssafely.

Use regular bombs to preserve ammo whenever you can, but don't be afraid to take the easy route and use Power Bombs when you have to.

Exit through the blue door to the left to find a Chozo Statue holding an Energy Tank!

Are you up for more? Again, the next path is easier later, but since you're here and you've got full health now...

Bomb or Power Bomb the girder to the right of the Chozo Statue, then drop down and bomb the block. You have to move fast if you use regular bombs and you will certainly take damage.

Roll to the left and emerge in a room with metal pillars. Shoot the one to the left to open the path.

What follows is a bit of a repeat -- a moving acid pool with rock pillars that can be bombed. You can get close to the first and second one and stand on the edge without taking damage.

The last one requires you to move fast, however, as lingering in front of it will certainly damage you. A Power Bomb will take care of it easily, but you need to make sure that you have at least one left for the final obstacle.

Wait until the acid is just above the first metal block to the left, jump over to it, keep heading left and drop a power bomb to destroy the metal spikes and wall on the left side of the chamber.

The last platform to the left is safe, except for the Maw above and a spawn pipe with Zebs flying out of it.

Open the blue door. But don't rush through the next room. There are brittle blocks ahead.

Basically, there are two Missile Expansions waiting below, but you cannot easily get them in one go.

There is a well of brittle blocks at the center that can only be broken by standing on them, but the walls that protect the two tanks can be shot with your Beam.

We'll get the left one for now and leave the second one for a future visit when you've got a new power that makes the experience very different.

When entering the room, blast away the blocks in front of you to create a horizontal opening. Basically, bricks four and five (each two regular blocks wide) from the right are brittle and will break when you step on them.

If you want the left Missile Tank, hop across the first brittle block and stand on the left. The blocks will break and you will descend downward.

When you're near the Missile Tank, blast to the left and create an opening to jump over to it.

As you drop, note that there are two hidden Beetoms behind destructible blocks to the left and the right.

You can bomb or shoot the floor in the center to drop down, then roll to the left to fall through more brittle blocks or use a Power Bomb to create an opening on the right side.

The blue door to the right leads back up the slanted cave where you found your first Energy Tank. Let's take that path, this time, so we can pick up some more collectibles.

Run up the ramp and enter the blue door. Blow up the wall.

Drop down the first cave opening and go to the bottom of the vertical cave with all the Geemers.

Open the blue hatch at the bottom and drop down the long shaft with the Space Pirates, as well.

You're in the room from the very beginning, where the battle with Mother Brain took place in the Metroid 1 flashbacks. There are Space Pirates here.

You have bombs now, so bomb the area under where the glass tank with Mother Brain sat to find a secret passage and another few bombable blocks.

Drop into a hidden chamber below to find another Missile Expansion.

We'll have to take another detour to get an Energy Tank.

Shoot all the Space Pirates to open the doors, then exit this room to the right and catch the elevator down to Brinstar.

Remember the end of the cave to the right, where a watchful eye couldn't stop you from snagging a Missile Tank? There's an Energy Tank there, too.

Head right from the elevator until you get to the blue room with the overhanging blocks.

Seven blocks to the left, from the overhang, there's an Energy Tank embedded in the ceiling. Shoot the ceiling, then use your Hi-Jump to grab it.

articles.title: Clayface Comes in Second to You Can See Everything at the Domestic Box Office on Halloween Weekend
articles.summary: Clayface has come in second at the domestic box office on the Halloween weekend as audiences continue to show up for Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything.
articles.body:
Clayface has come in second at the domestic box office on the Halloween weekend as audiences continue to show up for Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything .

It was a narrow victory for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's comedic look into the life of the controversial Theranos creator, thanks to an estimated haul of $10.6 million to the DCU movie's $10.4 million (Note: These positions could change once final totals are tallied Monday). You Can See Everything's limited international rollout means Clayface is comfortably first globally ($22.8 million), but in what is technically the doc's third weekend in theaters, becoming the number one movie in the domestic market is still an impressive feat.

It's less of a warning of how audiences feel about Clayface and more of a sign that the behind-the-scenes peek at Holmes' life has real staying power. Originally released to just 855 theaters October 16, the Fielder doc has benefited from strong word-of-mouth and stellar reviews (IGN gave it a 10/10 ). Movie social media platform Letterboxd even pointed out that the project quickly emerged as its highest-rated feature film ever , with its first weekend in theaters landing it in second behind Street Fighter .

Returning with more auditoriums under its belt, You Can See Everything came in second again when Clayface brought moviegoers to a new Gotham City for its debut last weekend . With the spooky holiday bolstering the atmosphere, many wondered if DC's body horror movie could fend off the competition for Halloween, but at this point, at least, Holmes' story persevered.

Really, though, both films performed well over the past three days. Domestically, after a box office increase in its second weekend, You Can See Everything dropped just 43%, while Clayface returned for its second bout with a drop of 57%. Both have relatively modest budgets, too, with the former packing a reported budget of less than $20 million when factoring in both production and marketing costs, while the latter is believed to have a $44 million production budget. You Can See Everything has accumulated $64 million thus far, with Clayface's global total standing at $82.9 million.

Clayface brings an often overlooked Batman villain to the big screen with a tragic backstory starring Tom Rhys Harries and Naomi Ackie. It also marked an important moment for DC Studios' DCU, which suffered some setbacks after Supergirl failed to successfully follow up on 2025's Superman when it premiered earlier this year. Even if it's not a home run, the villain origin movie seems to have done its job so far, with the weeks ahead sure to keep increasing its total theatrical haul.

Meanwhile, at the worldwide box office, Resident Evil jumped from coming in fifth last weekend to being fourth for Halloween. The Zach Cregger video game adaptation has now reached $400 million against its reported $75 million budget. There's also Laika's critically acclaimed Wildwood, which is still trying to make a dent in its reported $100 million budget. Its worldwide pull for the weekend was $11.54 million, bringing its total after two weekends to $35.17 million.

Some of October's biggest releases arrived earlier in the month, but moviegoers have an even spread of headliners to look forward to in the weeks ahead. Director Takashi Yamazaki's kaiju sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero , stomps into theaters November 6 (or earlier if you're looking to catch a Godzilla Day showing November 3). I Play Rocky will offer a new perspective on a classic sports drama this weekend, too, with The Cat in the Hat also set to release then.

Denis Villeneuve's first two Dune movies get the re-release treatment November 13 as viewers prep for Part 3 . Then, come November 20, there's the latest Hunger Games prequel film, Sunrise on the Reaping . Focker In-Law stars Ben Stiller, Ariana Grande, Robert De Niro, and Skyler Gisondo November 25.

For more while we wait for the 2026 movie slate to finish up, you can check out IGN's 7/10 review of Clayface . You can also check out our latest opinion piece for You Can See Everything , but then be sure to check out our top-rated movies of the year so far .

articles.title: Dread Honcho Walkthrough - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: ”Dread Honcho” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks after Anai’s Visitor Quest, “Stress Free,” has been completed in Hello Kitty
articles.body:
”Dread Honcho” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks after Anai’s Visitor Quest, “Stress Free,” has been completed in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . Once this quest is complete, you’ll be able to invite a new person to the island.

To start the quest, you’ll need to talk to Retsuko , who can usually be found in the Hot Springs of Mount Hothead . She’s relieved to see you! Chief Komiya has organized a meeting, and Retsuko is looking for an excuse to get out of it. You don’t have anything immediate that needs doing, but maybe Fenneko can help! Follow Retsuko to find her sleuthy friend!

Fenneko and Haida will be hanging out just south of the Hot Springs. Talk to Fenneko to see what ideas she has accrued. Oh, she’s.. not letting Retsuko get away with it. Retsuko invites you along as moral support, and Haida looks at the bright side. Maybe there will be some free donuts or pizza.

Attend the office meeting without the office and follow the crew to the Hot Springs, in an area just outside of Visitor Cabin 2. You notice that Chief Komiya has gathered all of Retsuko’s coworkers to hear out his announcement.

As you might have suspected, Chief Komiya is ready to welcome Director Ton to the island! But first, he’ll need a proper welcoming party! Which is why he has gathered everyone here.

The office party is split on levels of enthusiasm, and Chief Komiya reiterates that he can’t simply take back his invite. In fact, he’s prepared a red carpet just for Director Ton’s arrival. He gives you a free Red Square Rug , the Crafting Plan for the Square Rug, and 5x Red Dye Pouches. Just in case you want to make more.

Retsuko relents. She is technically in charge of logistics, so she should help out with the planning. Haida and Fenneko are participating in a rage moment, but… none comes. Somehow that’s more worrying.

Retsuko pardons herself to go on a walk. Follow after her to make sure that she’s okay. Retsuko can be found on the beach, south of Mount Hothead’s Mailbox . She scoffs at all the work Chief Komiya is going through to welcome Director Ton, but she’s got bigger priorities. There’s a secret gathering happening at the top of Gemstone Mountain .

Follow Retsuko to the Gemstone Corral Mailbox at the top of the mountain and meet up with Haida and Fenneko just behind the Mailbox. You’ve officially joined the Anti-Ton Team. You have gone through so much to try and make sure that Director Ton doesn’t visit the island, but now the inevitable is happening.

Haida plans on disappearing, and Fenneko plans on avoiding him in general. Retsuko claims that that’s not a great approach to their new visitor. Her concern is no longer with the stress of Director Ton’s visit, but how he deals with her new friends she’s made on the island.

She is prepared to enact Operation Boss Battle to make sure that Director Ton does not bully any of the other residents on the island! Before you can go into details, Chococat appears to ask what you are up to. He needs some help from Retsuko and the others for some research he’s been doing on Mount Hothead.

Fenneko and Haida excuse themselves to work on Operation Boss Battle, and Retsuko explains that she’s helping her friends right now, but will check back in with Chococat once her original plans are completed. Head to Spooky Swamp to find out what ideas Fenneko and Haida have come up with to make sure Director Ton does not disrupt the peace on Friendship Island.

Fenneko is gathering information from Gori and Washimi to find out what she can do to run interference on Director Ton.

Head to Merry Meadows next to talk to Haida and find out what he’s thought up. He tried roping in Anai , but the young man has dipped out. Ookami , however, is willing to help out in organizing a Boys Club! This will make sure that Director Ton has no time to bother anyone else, because the club will have tons of activities and sports talk!

With some ideas in place, all you need to know now is when Director Ton is set to arrive. Go check in with Kabae and Chief Komiya, all sneaky-like, to find out when Director Ton is arriving.

Head to Gemstone Mountain to hang out at the Dance Hall, in hopes of being able to listen in on Chief Komiya’s planning. After hiding behind a barrel, you’ll find out that Director Ton is heading to the island right now!

Retreat to Retsuko immediately! She can be found at the Seaside Resort beach just south of the Mailbox near the plaza. Just as soon as you can relay the information, Fenneko drops by with a terrifying announcement. HE’S HERE!

Without even a second to breathe, Director Ton stomps over and looks directly at you, demanding to know where his cabin is. Well… so much for all that planning. What’s most important now is preparing a visitor cabin for Director Ton.

With “Dread Honcho” complete, you can begin preparing a visitor cabin for Director Ton in Mount Hothead. Below are all of the specific requirements he’ll need for furnishing.

articles.title: Zach Cregger Was 'Frustrated' the Conversation Around Resident Evil 'Didn't Have Anything to Do With the Movie'
articles.summary: Horror filmmaker Zach Cregger has explained why he was "frustrated" that much of the conversation around his Resident Evil film "didn't have anything to do with the movie."
articles.body:
Horror filmmaker Zach Cregger has explained why he was "frustrated" that much of the conversation around his Resident Evil film "didn't have anything to do with the movie."

The mind behind hits like Barbarian and Weapons touched on his feelings about the lead-up to the premiere of his latest project during an appearance on The Town with Matthew Belloni podcast. Anyone who paid a second of attention to the Resident Evil movie adaptation knows Cregger struggled to win fans over ahead of its release, and it's something that left him frustrated from a number of angles.

"I think I was frustrated at the conversation around Resident Evil and how much of the conversation really didn't have anything to do with the movie," he said when explaining why he will likely stray from making movies based on established IP in the future.

"It had everything to do with whether the movie was living up to the different standards that different fans of the games had. Whether it was using the characters or not, or what did I get wrong in the lore? It was just a lot about, 'Why isn't this like the source material, or why is it good that it's not like the source material? All the conversation just felt like it was about not the movie."

Skeptical viewers harped on most of the same topics between the release of Resident Evil's first trailer and its theatrical premiere. Where's Leon? Why is it snowing in Raccoon City? Why does Austin Abrams' character have a smartphone? This vocal group of fans spent most of their time worried about what the film meant for the games it was based on and less about how it might carve out its own place in Capcom's wider universe.

Although Cregger did his best to explain that he took creative liberties to improve the overall quality of the movie, he did little to calm the storm of those who have longed to see the faces and places they know and love on the big screen. He did eventually go on to admit he was naïve to assume there would be any other outcome, but uncertain fans remained uneasy about what the final product might look like all the way up until its September 18 release date.

So, how did it do? Despite the backlash, it was a tremendous hit, and it's one Cregger is proud of.

The average movie fan who went to see Resident Evil was generally happy with a new, snowy vision of Raccoon City, too. The film premiered to great reviews (IGN gave it an 8/10 ) and opened to a whopping $108 million at the worldwide box office.

With a reported budget of $75 million, that was already a solid start, but audiences also continued to show up for the movie in the weeks that followed. Now, as the Halloween weekend draws to a close, Resident Evil has managed to cross $400 million across the globe. That's probably enough success to convince Sony to bring Cregger back for a sequel, but it may be best to keep expectations on that front low for now.

"I'm proud of the movie. I really love the movie," Cregger elaborated during the podcast appearance. "I realize I should have known better going into it. I should have understood that was going to be the case, but for some reason, I was a little shocked."

Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond

Did Cregger say he had ideas for a Resident Evil 2? Yes . Did he say he wanted to step away from franchise films after this one came out? Also yes . Now that the dust is starting to settle after fans spent months upset about his vision for the series, he has suggested he's not terribly interested in carrying the weight of an existing IP. Still, for him, it's a "never say never" situation.

The conversation around Resident Evil may have given Cregger more than he bargained for, so we'll have to wait to see what happens next. In the meantime, he's tinkering away on his next original film, The Flood . A sci-fi thriller written, produced, and directed by Cregger, the movie will star Hunger Games veteran Jennifer Lawrence when it premieres August 11, 2028.

While we wait for updates, you can read about how the Resident Evil movie boosted sales for Capcom's game series . Be sure to also read up on how watchers reacted to the film's divisive ending .

articles.title: Dave Bautista Reveals He's Gained 20 Pounds of Muscle to Play Kratos in the God of War Series
articles.summary: Dave Bautista Reveals He's Gained 20 Pounds of Muscle to Play Kratos in the God of War Series
articles.body:
Dave Bautista has revealed he's gained 20 pounds of muscle in preparation for his role as Kratos in Prime Video's God of War series.

The Guardians of the Galaxy star officially replaced Ryan Hurst in the role back in August, after Hurst tore a bicep during the filming of a stunt for the series and had to be withdrawn from the production due to the estimated length of his recovery. In early September, Bautista shared a video on Instagram flexing his improved physique, noting that he had been weight training for three weeks and had two months to "get where he needs to be."

Now it seems those two months are up, with Bautista sharing a new video to his Instagram story with the text "Gained 20 lbs for GOW" and a "250" sticker on it, indicating his current weight. The actor is also wearing a God of War t-shirt in the post.

Dave Bautista reveals he has gained 20 more pounds of muscle for playing Kratos in ‘GOD OF WAR’. He has now reached 250 pounds. — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) November 1, 2026

Dave Bautista reveals he has gained 20 more pounds of muscle for playing Kratos in ‘GOD OF WAR’. He has now reached 250 pounds.

Bautista, who maintained an average weight of 290 pounds during his WWE wrestling career, had previously lost a lot of his muscle mass in recent years in an effort to open up more diverse acting roles and feel more comfortable on camera. This caused him to slim down quite dramatically, to the point that some God of War fans questioned his suitability to play the musclebound spartan in the Prime Video series after his involvement was confirmed. However, this latest update from the newly buffed-up Bautista sure seems to have proved those naysayers wrong.

Prime Video's God of War series is set to be based on the Norse mythology era of the PlayStation videogame franchise, and will follow father and son Kratos (Bautista) and Atreus (Callum Vinson) as they embark on a journey to spread the ashes of their wife and mother, Faye, at the highest peak of the nine realms. Two seasons of the show have been ordered.

articles.title: How to Place Standing Tables - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: During the The Saw Turns Again Quest, you're taught how to run your first Facility. However, one particular popularity task at Timberhamd Sawmill requires
articles.body:
During the The Saw Turns Again Quest, you're taught how to run your first Facility. However, one particular popularity task at Timberhamd Sawmill requires you to place a standing table, but the instructions to do so aren't very clear. Here's exactly what you need to know about placing standing tables (waiting tables) in Crimson Desert's DLC, Charting the Unknown .

As you level up your Facility's popularity, you'll have to complete specific goals to reach higher levels. For the Timberham Sawmill, you'll need to fulfill the following objectives to reach level 2:

You'll need to read the book, The Courtesy of Waiting, to learn the Waiting Table recipe that the quest refers to as a Standing Table. You can find the 'The Courtesy of Waiting' crafting book in your Documents tab of your Inventory after reaching Popularity Level 1 . After doing so, head back to the Management menu and tap on the Place Installables button. Check the bottom right corner for the button prompt to open your Installables inventory.

Under the section that has an icon of a building and a chest, you'll find the Standing Table all the way to the right. You'll need at least 2,000 Camp Funds to place one inside the sawmill. After doing so, return to the previous menu and tap on Manage Goods. Now that you're at Popularity Lvl. 1, you'll have an extra slot for a second item to sell.

By default, you should have the Wood synergy task complete if you kept the default good here. Otherwise, you can select one with the Wood tag beneath its name. Adding a second item with the Wood tag will increase the synergy bonus. Then, as long as you keep the Selling Price bar in the green for a Favorable response, you'll satisfy three customers easily.

articles.title: The Occultist - Castlevania: Belmont's Curse Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Occultist, Carmilla, is the boss that you encounter during your playthrough of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse as you explore the Library. Rose will be
articles.body:
The Occultist, Carmilla, is the boss that you encounter during your playthrough of Castlevania: Belmont's Curse as you explore the Library . Rose will be facing off against this bloody foe as she reaches the top of the Observation Tower. Carmilla is completing a ritual to bring a permanent Blood Moon to the world, wrapping it in an eternal darkness for Dracula.

When the battle begins, Carmilla immediately puts Rose in a blood spell. This spell conjures an 8 above her, indicating how many hits you can take during this fight. If the number reaches zero, meaning you've been hit more than 8 times, Carmilla grabs Rose and ends the fight, regardless of how much health you have left.

At the beginning of the fight, Carmilla summons a pair of skulls to protect her similar to how Talos protected himself. You'll need to destroy these skulls to begin damaging her. You can attempt to aim at them one at a time, or you can try hitting them both to cause them to fall. A good way to do this would be with the Fist of Talos or the Holy Cross Arcana. These two work tremendously well during this encounter. You can only damage Carmilla when both skulls are destroyed.

Many of Carmilla's attacks in this fight come from the blood spouts that shoot up from the base of the blood pool. These spouts are massive and go to the ceiling of the arena, meaning you won't be able to merely jump out of the way. Similar to when you were fighting Joan , these pillars take up the entire screen, and you'll need to move out of the way to dodge them.

These blood spouts come in an array of patterns, many appearing in the previously safe spots that the last combo left open for you. You should expect to keep moving through this fight to dodge these attacks, but you don't want to go too far, as you run the risk of being too far away from Carmilla to damage her.

Carmilla does eventually reconjure the skulls to protect her, forcing you to break them again before you can damage her. Every so often, she dives into the pool of blood, appearing on the opposite side of the arena. You'll want to move around, watching the blood trail she leaves behind as she moves to indicate where she's going to pop up next.

Unlike the other bosses, Carmilla does not have a second phase. Many of her attacks remain the same. You won't have to do too much guesswork or relearning with her. Continue to keep the pressure on her and save your Arcana uses of her skulls, and she'll be defeated. You'll unlock her spell, Blood Spikes, along with getting the Paint Brush to bring back to the Main Hall, and unlock an Air Dash to unlock more locations for you to explore throughout the game.

articles.title: Sonos Play review: The Sonos to add first
articles.summary: The first thing the Sonos Play teaches you is where to hold it.
articles.body: The first thing the Sonos Play teaches you is where to hold it. Pick it up by the sides, the way the oval shape invites you to, and your fingers land on the power and Bluetooth buttons at the back. I cut the music twice on the first evening, carrying it from the living room to the kitchen. By day three I was reaching for the rubber loop without thinking, which is probably why the loop is there.It's a small thing, but it says a lot about the speaker. Sonos has never made much that you hold. Its speakers sit on shelves and under TVs and stay there. Even the Move 2, the one with a handle, weighs over 3kg, and most people only ever carried it as far as the balcony. The Play is 1.3kg and about the size of a hardback, and it's the first Sonos that seems designed to be picked up several times a day.And then Sonos gave it a job that needs it to sit absolutely still.I had a pair. By evening they sat at either end of the console table behind my sofa, filling in the rear channels for an Arc Ultra and a Sub 4. By morning, one of them had usually gone somewhere else. Rs 35,999 apiece is a lot to ask of a speaker doing three jobs at once, and I spent three weeks waiting for it to slip up at one of them.The job that needs it to sit stillThe first evening went mostly into finding a charger. Each Play comes with a charging base, its USB-C cable fixed in place, but no adapter in the box, and it wants at least 18W, or 45W to fill up quickly. The second base ended up running off my laptop charger and stayed that way for the rest of the review.The surround setup itself took a few minutes. Until recently, that console-table job wasn't on offer at all. Rear speakers for a Sonos soundbar meant speakers that stayed plugged in behind you for good. Sonos 27, the software update Sonos rolled out this autumn and now calls an audio operating system, changed that, and it lets a matched pair of Plays or Move 2s sit behind any of Sonos's current Arc or Beam soundbars. I picked the two Plays in the soundbar settings, set them down behind me, and they worked out between themselves which was left and which was right, using their microphones and a high-frequency signal I never heard. Everything talks over the home Wi-Fi, so the only cables behind my sofa were the ones going into the two bases. The app walking me through it is new too, rebuilt for Sonos 27 around three plain tabs after the 2024 redesign went badly, and it got me from unboxing to surround sound without once asking me to try again.The Daytona sequence early in F1 is where I stopped thinking about setup. The cars come from behind you, and the engine note travelled from the Plays to the Arc Ultra in one sweep, with no gap where one speaker handed over to the next. The sandworm ride in Dune: Part Two did something similar with sand instead of engines, the hiss and rumble closing in from behind before the Sub 4 took the floor out from under it. A couple of nights later I loaded Forza Horizon 5 on the Xbox and spent an hour checking my mirrors less. The car closing in on my rear-left was audible before it showed up in them.Even a Sunday morning Test match got better. Commentary stayed planted at the front with the Arc Ultra, while the crowd noise and the odd roar after a boundary wrapped around from behind, which made the living room feel a few rows closer to the ground.The Plays have it easy back there, and that suits them. Neither digs very deep into the bass on its own, but with a Sub 4 in the room, they never have to. All they need to do is place sound clearly at ear height, and by the end of the first week I'd stopped noticing them at all, which is about the best thing anyone can say about rear speakers.Then the film ends, and one of them goes to the kitchen. Lift a Play off the console table and it quietly drops out of the home theatre and becomes a regular speaker wherever you set it down. Bring it back, pause whatever's playing, and it rejoins as a surround. I kept expecting this to need a trip into the app at some point over the three weeks. It never did.The kitchen at 11pmThe kitchen is where I found out what a single Play sounds like, mostly late at night, mostly over the washing up. Arooj Aftab's "Mohabbat" is mostly voice and empty space, and the two angled tweeters left that space alone, which cheaper speakers rarely manage. Lucky Ali's "O Sanam" came through warm and close, his voice pushed forward the way Sonos tunes almost everything, with the guitar clean around it. Amit Trivedi's "Iktara" had the same intimacy, Kavita Seth's voice sitting right at the front with the strings unhurried behind her.Bass is tight and well timed rather than deep. The bassline on Khruangbin's "Maria También" kept its bounce off the single midwoofer, but the bottom of it fades out sooner than the room asked for, and the Move 2 goes noticeably lower if that matters to you. The two passive radiators push against each other, so even at higher volume the speaker never buzzed or crept across the counter. I nudged the bass slider up two notches and left it there. Bass and treble are the only two sliders Sonos gives you, and that would matter later.One night I'd started "Iktara" from the Sonos app, walked to the bedroom with my phone, and only realised halfway there that the kitchen hadn't gone quiet. On Wi-Fi, the Play pulls music straight off the internet itself, from the Sonos app, Spotify Connect or AirPlay 2, rather than streaming it from your phone, so the song carried on without me. The controls followed me anyway. Sonos 27 puts them on the iPhone lock screen and in the Dynamic Island, and by the second week I was turning the kitchen down from the bedroom without opening anything.Most of those evenings it sat a foot from the sink, and the IP67 rating turned the splashes into a non-event. There were more of them than I'd like to admit. Moving it from the tiled counter to the bedroom bookshelf changed nothing I could hear, which is Automatic Trueplay listening to each room through the microphones and adjusting on its own. I only caught it working when I flipped the mic switch on the back and the kitchen version turned thin and slightly brittle. The same microphones run Sonos Voice Control and Alexa, and with dough on both hands, "Hey Sonos, skip" earned its keep. There's no Google Assistant, though, and for all those microphones, no speakerphone either. When my phone rang mid-song, I was still drying my hands to answer it.Where one runs out of roomThose two EQ sliders came back to bother me on the second Sunday, with friends over. Coke Studio Bharat's "Khalasi" is loud and busy by design, and somewhere past 80% volume the Play's upper mids turned hard and shouty, the kind of edge that makes people raise their voices instead of enjoying the song. A midrange slider would have fixed it. Without one, I brought the volume back to around 60%, where it settled and still filled the living room with room to spare.By evening I'd paired the two in stereo, and the afternoon's complaint stopped mattering. Pink Floyd's "Money" finally did what it's supposed to, the cash register sounds walking from one side of the room to the other, something a lone Play can't do however its tweeters are angled. Tame Impala's "Let It Happen" was better still, the synths swirling across the full width of the room while Kevin Parker's voice held the middle. Two Plays at 50% did more for the room than one at 80% ever could.From then on, weekend mornings were stereo pair and weeknights were surrounds, and switching between the two never took more than a tap.The furthest it wentThe furthest either Play went was a friend's terrace the last week, and it was there that it made the best case for itself as a portable speaker. One press of the Bluetooth button on the back took it off my home Wi-Fi and onto my phone in a few seconds, and holding play/pause on the second one pulled it into the same song. Sonos now lets up to four Plays or Move 2s group this way, which it never allowed before. The phone talks to one speaker over Bluetooth while the speakers keep each other in sync over a direct Wi-Fi link of their own, and I couldn't hear any lag between them. They play the same signal rather than splitting into left and right, and outdoors nobody could tell.Automatic Trueplay kept up there too. Out in the open, where most speakers turn thin, Bayaan's "Maand" kept its warmth, and Diljit Dosanjh's "Born to Shine" had enough low end to carry across the terrace without anyone asking for it to go up. For a speaker this size, it filled the space comfortably, and that evening nobody once asked whose speaker it was because it sounded small.Sonos rates the 35Wh battery at 24 hours at moderate volume. At the couple of hours a day I played it away from the base, that worked out to almost a week, and the Play went back on charge on Saturday mornings more out of habit than need. Someone's phone got topped up from its USB-C port that night on the terrace, the same port that takes Sonos's Line-In Adapter if a record player needs a speaker. And since the owner can replace the battery, a few years from now a tired cell means a new battery rather than a new speaker.Back home, the same songs sounded a touch cleaner on Wi-Fi than on Bluetooth, which only offers SBC and AAC, though I had to switch back and forth to be sure. It's heavy enough that it went in the car, never in a bag. For everywhere it actually went, that was enough.Still behind the sofaOn its own, the Play is a portable I’d happily live with. It sat by a kitchen sink for three weeks without complaint, held its own on a terrace with nobody asking for it to go louder, and only went back on charge on Saturday mornings. The compromises are small ones you work around rather than live with: a charger you have to find yourself, a weight that keeps it out of your bag, and a top end that wants the volume kept under 80%.Still, Rs 35,999 is a lot for one speaker, but it’s a price you can live with. Two cost Rs 71,998, which is a lot to spend on rear speakers, except rear speakers usually do nothing for the rest of the day, except rear speakers usually do nothing for the rest of the day, and a portable usually does nothing for your home theatre. This pair did both. If they were never going to leave the room, two Era 100s would be more affordable and slightly smoother choice. The Play makes sense because it moves, and in my house it moved almost every day.Three weeks later, I was still waiting for it to slip up at one of those jobs. The pair went from rear surrounds to a stereo pair to a kitchen speaker to someone else’s terrace, and every evening both were back on their bases behind the sofa before the film started. Sonos 27 is what gave the Play that third job, and in a house already running an Arc Ultra or a Beam, that makes it the Sonos to add first. Just hold it by the loopOur rating: 4/5You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Part 4: 2026-27 SoCon Preview: The lower tier and the longshots
articles.summary: Tennessee Tech joins the league. The Citadel has promise, and UNCG welcomes in a new coach
articles.body:
The final portion of the 2026-27 Mid-Major Madness preview series for SoCon basketball takes a look at three unique situations, with newcomer Tennessee Tech introducing an new unknown into the equation, and with a loaded roster, the Golden Eagles will without question compete right away, but can they handle the rigors of a road environment on a random Wednesday night in the SoCon at Cameron Hall or Timmons Arena?

What about the home atmosphere? Can the Hooper-Eblen Center keep on par with a majority of the league's other home venues and become an intimidating fortress?

Then, there is The Citadel, which brings perhaps more momentum into a season than it has in over a decade since the last time Ed Conroy was the head coach. The Bulldogs have put together their most talented portal class to date under Conroy, and if preseason results are any indicator of projected success, than being a "long shot" in this tough league might be much too low of expectation for The Citadel in 2026-27. Still, as talented as the Bulldogs are, they have to go out and prove that they are the real deal and not the Bulldogs we've known so many times before.

Finally, UNCG brings a new coach on-board, in Jerod Haase, and the big question is can this program recover its status as being a perennial title contender, and if so, how long will it take Haase to build that strong foundation and rebuild that winning culture that the Spartans were able to build and sustain under Wes Miller and Mike Jones for the past 11 seasons, winning 233 games, which is the second most wins only to Furman's 245 victories in that same span.

Change is something that has been needed for a long time in Cookeville for the men's basketball program at Tennessee Tech.

The dominoes started to fall in favor of change even before the 2025-26 season when it was announced in July 2025 that the Golden Eagles would be joining the SoCon as its newest league member. Then came the 2025-26 season for the Golden Eagles, which would turn out to be a very disappointing one in their final season in the OVC.

It was out with a whimper, as the Golden Eagles failed to qualify for even the OVC Tournament, as Tech finished one place out of being eligible for the conference tournament. That led to the dismissal of former head coach John Pelphrey and the naming of Tobin Anderson as the head coach in the spring. TTU also renovated its locker rooms at the Hooper-Eblen Center.

For a program that hasn't made an NCAA Tournament appearance since 1963 and entering a conference that is traditionally much stronger on the hardwood than the one it called home, Tennessee Tech showed it has become the place to be for recruits and that has a lot to do with a forward-thinking administration.

Only two regulars returned to the fold from the previous edition of Golden Eagles basketball: forward Mekhi Turner (4.2 PPG, 2.8 RPG) and guard Ty Owens (6.7 PPG, 2.5 RPG). Those two players will be pillars for the new head coach to lean on this season.

Both Turner and Owens figure to play much bigger roles this season for the Golden Eagles. For Anderson, Tennessee Tech represents a second chance after he was unceremoniously let go after two years at Iona following a season in which he led the Gaels all the way to the championship game of the MAAC.

Anderson spent a season as a top assistant at South Florida under Bryan Hodgson, helping South Florida to an American Conference title. He was announced as Tech's new head coach just before USF's conference tournament title run.

Anderson detailed how much the year as an assistant under Hodgson helped him learn a new system, which was influenced by Nate Oats' system at Alabama due to Hodgson's time coaching with Oats in Tuscaloosa.

The Golden Eagles have athleticism and talent acquired from the portal, and under Anderson, the Golden Eagles will be a little bit like the newest version of Bucky Ball in the SoCon, which if you don't know the reference, it was a style of play that was utilized by Samford of full-court pressure to influence tempo and create chaos over a five-year span from 2020-25 when Bucky McMillan was the head coach there in Homewood.

Tennessee Tech will be one of the more athletic teams in the SoCon in the coming season, and if there's a name you need to know, it's Davante Hackett, who comes to Cookeville having already established himself as a big-time scoring threat. The Stonehill transfer started 11 of 33 games for the Hawks last season, averaging 13.6 PPG, 1.5 APG and 4.1 RPG.

The 6-foot-3 senior point guard will have one year of eligibility remaining after putting together a solid 2025-26 season, which saw him score in double figures in 21 of 33 games for the Hawks last season, including scoring a combined 132 points in the final five games of the season, averaging 26.4 PPG in those final five games of the season. That included setting the program's new NCAA Division-I milestone by posting 40 points against Saint Francis on Feb. 26. In the 103-77 win over the Red Flash, Hackett connected on 14-of-24 shots from the field, including going 8-for-14 from 3-point range.

Staying in the backcourt, Cbo Newton will also have a chance to have an immediate impact for the Golden Eagles in year one, as he transferred into the program from a reputable Division-I program, Abilene Christian. The 6-foot-3 redshirt junior point guard could be in the mix for major playing time this coming season.

He started in 24 games in his lone season with the Wildcats last season, and he ended up averaging 10.1 PPG, 2.2 RPG and 1.2 APG. Newton is a physical point guard who can score at all three levels and figures to a key contender for a starting spot at point guard.

The next player to be aware of is another point guard, with the diminutive 5-foot-9 Cohenj Gonzales transferring in from Colorado Mesa. Prior to that, he spent his first two seasons at Pima Community College.

During his two seasons spent at Pima CC, he was an all-conference selection as both a freshman and sophomore. In his sophomore season, he averaged 18.4 PPG and started all 32 games, while shooting a strong 38.5% from 3-point range.

He was both freshman of the year and conference player of the year during his two seasons at Pima, helping his program to a third-place finish in the 2023-24 NJCAA Division II Championship. In addition to those accolades, he was also a NJCAA All-American selection in both seasons.

In his one season at Colorado Mesa, Gonzales finished the season averaging 10.6 PPG and found his way into double figures in 18 of 31 games last season for the Mavericks. Gonzales was one of the team's top perimeter threats last season, connecting on an impressive 42% (55-of-131) from 3-point range. He saw action in 31 games, garnering 22 starts.

Gonzales was also an outstanding free throw shooter, as he completed the season by connecting at an 88.9% (48-of-54) clip from the charity stripe. He also added 2.2 RPG last season, while dishing out a total of 83 assists. He'll also be another valuable piece in the rotation at the point guard position.

Combo guard Trent Mosquera comes aboard from Le Moyne and will add a "glue guy" vibe, as he is a gritty, tough defender, as well as being accomplished on the backboards where he averaged almost six boards per game (5.8 RPG) last season.

Mosquera's ability to step out and be a 3-point threat for the Golden Eagles will be key this season. His scoring ability, consistency and leadership were all reasons the new head coach brought him into this collection of talent.

In his final of three seasons at Le Moyne last season, Mosquera started 30 of 32 games, helping the Dolphins to a 15-17 mark in what was its third season in Division I. He ranked second on the team in scoring, averaging 13.5 PPG, and he finished the season as one of the best perimeter shooters in the NEC, knocking down an impressive 40.4% from 3-point range (77-of-219) last season.

Caleb Hollenbeck is a 6-foot-4 guard who comes about with one year of eligibility remaining after having spent one season with the Marshall Thundering Herd in the Sun Belt Conference. Before that, he played two seasons at Gillette College. In his one season spent in Huntington, W.Va., playing for the Thundering Herd, he started 27 of 32 games, averaging 5.7 PPG, 1.6 RPG and one APG last season.

Hollenbeck enjoyed his best game of the season against West Virginia Tech last season, as he posted a 25-point outing. Hollenbeck will figure into the mix as a 3-point specialist for the Golden Eagles in the upcoming season, as he comes off a solid first season of Division-I basketball, connecting on 39.7% (54-of-136) from 3-point range. Hollenbeck finished his one season in Huntington with just seven 2-point field goals.

A big man that joins Anderson in making the transition from South Florida is 6-foot-10 power forward De'Ante Green. The Asheville, N.C., native arrives in Cookeville having had an injury-plagued career, which is the primary reason Green did not see any action during the 2025-26. As a junior in 2024-25, Green logged action in 21 contests, including four starts before suffering that season-ending injury. He's looking to make the most in his final season of ball, and like Anderson, he'll be looking to make the most of this "second-chance" opportunity.

As for comparisons for Green go, although a little older, he reminds me a little of former Mercer big man Armani Mighty from last season. He has similar size and athleticism to that of the former Mercer all-conference big man from last season.

Another player from South Florida is 6-foot-6 forward Caleb Sanders. He logged action in 11 games and made a pair of starts in his rookie season with the Bulls. Sanders scored in six out of the 11 games he logged action in, highlighted by his 12-point outing on 4-of-7 shooting from 3-point land in a win over Coppin State. He posted eight points, five rebounds and four assists in his USF debut in a win over Florida A&M. Sanders is a good shooter on the wing and could also prove to be an effect asset on the defensive end with his length and athleticism.

Shaun Arnold (Thomas Aquinas/Univ. of Indianapolis), Dane Christensen (Gillette College/Texas Rio Grande Valley) and Kyler Fox (Itawamba CC) round out the front court portal additions.

Fox comes to Tennessee Tech following one season at the JUCO level at Itawamba CC and averaged 7.7 PPG and 7.7 RPG in 31 games, including 28 starts during his rookie campaign. Fox knows how to finish around the basket, as evidenced by his eye-popping 71.4% field goal clip he turned in during his freshman campaign, connecting on 101-of-141 shots for the season. The 6-foot-8 power forward is an above the rim type player and is a quick leaper. He could also prove effective on the defensive end as a rim protector. Fox will have three years of eligibility remaining entering the 2026-27 campaign.

Arnold, who is a 6-foot-5 small forward from Division-II University of Indianapolis, will have one year of eligibility remaining. He figures to be a player in line to see rotational minutes as well for the Golden Eagles, as he averaged an impressive 11.3 PPG, 8.9 RPG, 2.9 APG, and 2.9 SPG at Indy. He showed the well-roundedness of his game on both ends of the floor with those statistical outputs in 2025-26.

He logged starts in 21 of the 22 games he saw action in last season, posting 16 double-figure scoring games, including four games with 20 or more points. Like Hackett at Stonehill in 2025-26, Arnold was particularly impressive down the stretch for UIndy last season, scoring 12, 22 and 21 points, respectively, in his final three games of the season. The rising senior spent his first two seasons as a college basketball player at Thomas Aquinas, ranking second on the team in scoring and third in rebounding in helping his previous school to the East Regional Championship.

Christensen was a teammate of Hollenbeck's during his time at Gillette, as the two now re-unite a second time in their careers in Cookeville. Christensen followed a similar tract to that of Hollenbeck, spending the 2025-26 season at the NCAA Division-I level, as he suited up for the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley, averaging 3.7 PPG and 2.5 RPG, as he saw action in 24 games, which included making three starts as a sophomore last season.

The Orem, Utah, native enjoyed his best outing of the season against Southwestern Adventist, scoring 17 points in a UTRGV win. In his freshman campaign at Gillette in 2024-25, Christiansen averaged 16.9 PPG and 7.3 RPG, connecting on 49.6% from the field and 40.7% from 3-point land.

The freshman newcomer you should be aware of coming into the season is 6-foot-2 guard Kamai Samuels, who was Anderson's first signed recruit upon arrival in Cookeville. Samuels is one of the most impressive freshman signees in the SoCon coming into the 2026-27 season, choosing Tennessee Tech among offers from Mississippi State, Penn State, Arizona State and California as a sophomore in high school. He also held offers from Sacred Heart, Fordham, UTEP and Iona before ultimately deciding upon Tech.

The other two additions to the team who have the potential to be real impact players as freshmen in 2026-27 are 5-foot-9 point guard Jake Pampolina out of Suffern, N.Y., by way of Suffern High School, as well as 6-foot-2 guard Harrison Stewart out of Spain Park High School in Birmingham, Ala.

Final Verdict for the Golden Eagles: Having Tobin Anderson in the SoCon is the blessing the league didn't know it needed, and his addition as the new head coach at Tennessee Tech last spring furthers the narrative of the SoCon as being its own cradle of coaches of sorts, as yet another coach with great energy, personality and a unique style and ability is introduced into a league already chocked full of coaching talent. Anderson has already provided the Golden Eagles with what they will need to more than hold their own in the always tough SoCon.
